items.title: North-East govs to float North-East Air, unveil 11-point communique in Borno
items.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The North-East Governors Forum (NEGF) on Saturday unveiled an 11-point communique at the end of its 13th regular meeting which took place in Maiduguri, the Borno state capital. Floating the North-East Air shuttle was part of the resolutions reached.. The governors unanimously recommitted to speaking with one voice and acting with one purpose on matters of common subregional concerns as they relate to security, social, economic integration and development. The meeting was Chaired by Professor Babagana Umara Zulum who is also the Chairman of the NEGF and Chief Host. Present at the meeting were governors Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri (Adamawa state), Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya (Gombe), Mohammed Auwal Jatau (Deputy Governor of Bauchi state), representing the governor, and Idi Barde Gubana, Deputy Governor of Yobe state, representing the governor of Yobe state. Their counterpart from Taraba was absent – and including his deputy. Also in attendance was the Deputy Governor of Borno state, Umar Usman Kadafur. Reading out the Communique at the end of their deliberations, Adamawa State Governor, Fintiri, said the Forum continues to appreciate the level of cooperation and collaboration among member-states since its inaugural meeting in Gombe in March 2020. He said the forum’s role remains a work in progress. The following communiqué was presented at the end of the meeting: “Forum notes the tremendous achievements it has made in the last six years, noting that the most significant achievement was the unity of forum members, resulting in the Forum delivering tangible result in the infrastructural development of the subregion. “Forum appreciates Mr. President for the renewed attention on the Port Harcourt–Jos–Bauchi–Gombe-Maiduguri rail corridor and frontier oil exploration at Kolmani and the Akwanga–Jos–Bauchi–Gombe–Biu–Maiduguri highway. “Forum however, calls on Federal Government to revisit the exploration activities earlier commenced but subsequently stalled in Magumeri and Gubio Local Government Areas of Borno State. “Forum acknowledges the concerted effort made by member states in providing power and energizing the subregion. It has moved the energy agenda from isolated state concerns to a regional energy agenda. The Dadinkowa hydropower plant now feeds the national grid. It encourages all member states to take advantage of the new electricity law and abundant sunshine to strengthen the electricity needs of the subregion and expanding solar and mini-grid solutions for development. “Forum reiterates its long-standing concern over the seeming neglect of the Mambila Hydro power plant and call on the Federal Government to take advantage of the recent clearance of the legal encumbrance with the the arbitration ruling on the matter, to expedite action on the completion and take-off of the plant. “Forum acknowledges the intervention role of the North East Development Commisssion (NEDC), in the Subregion. It calls for more investment in the Education sector, especially the release of the long-awaited scholarship awards to indigent students of the subregion and deploying more resource into the campaign for reducing the burden of out of school children and a coordinated support for the Tsangaya education. To ease the cost of transportation, strengthen logistics and open the region to more economic activities, Forum agreed to partner with Green Ville Energy to build and provide more CNG and LNG stations within the region. “Forum equally acknowledges and appreciates the support of the Federal Government through the NEDC in providing 10,000 Electric Tricycles, 10 Electric Buses and 300 Electric Taxes with a view to lessening the burden of transportation, to be launched in October. “Forum acknowledges the appreciable success recorded in the onslaught against the insurgency in the north- East; the courage and sacrifice of the Armed Forces and other security agencies, the resilience of the people and the commitment of Governments at all levels, but regrets that the subregion is still confronted by daunting humanitarian and infrastructural challenges. Forum thus, reaffirm its commitment to supporting the Armed Forces and other security agencies while strengthening inter-State cooperation, intelligence sharing, community engagement and coordinated responses to emerging threats and at the same time, addressing the underlying socio-economic conditions that can expose the young people to exploitation by criminal and extremist elements. “Forum acknowledges that the North-East has one of the youngest populations in the country, and this represents both an enormous opportunity and a responsibility. “Forum Therefore, recommit to equipping the young people with quality education, vocational and entrepreneurial skills, technology and meaningful employment opportunities for a secure and prosperous region where the youth see a future for themselves and have legitimate opportunities to build dignified livelihoods. “Forum decries the quantum of harm done to the environment through deforestation and agrees to partner with the Institute of Forest Research to train forest experts in the region. “The next meeting is to hold on 18th – 19th December, 2026 at Gombe, Gombe state”. Fintiri explained on behalf of the NEGF Chairman, Professor Zulum.” Vanguard News The post North-East govs to float North-East Air, unveil 11-point communique in Borno appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Train Alger – Tamanrasset : l’Algérie se prépare à lancer un chantier ferroviaire de 1000 km
items.description: L’Algérie mise sur le chemin de fer pour désenclaver les vastes régions du Sud du pays et exploiter de grands gisements miniers à l’Est et à l’Ouest. Après avoir construit la ligne ferroviaire reliant le gisement de minerai de fer de Gara Djebilet à Béchar sur 950 km et lancé le chantier de la voie ferrée minière de l’Est entre le gisement de phosphate de Blad el Habda et Annaba, le gouvernement s’intéresse au train Alger – Tamanrasset . Ce projet consiste à relier par train la capitale à l’extrême Sud du pays sur plus de 2.000 km et est classé comme « stratégique et prioritaire » par le président Abdelmadjid Tebboune. « Les efforts doivent être concentrés sur son achèvement dans les délais impartis, avec une mise en service prévue fin 2028, ce qui constituerait une réalisation historique sans précédent pour l’Algérie », a fixé le chef de l’État lors de la réunion du Conseil des ministres du 6 septembre dernier. Train Alger – Tamanrasset : deux géants chinois du BTP impliqués Pour atteindre cet objectif, le gouvernement accélère les préparatifs pour mettre en chantier 1.000 km de chemins de fer de cette ligne. Il s’agit des tronçons reliant Laghouat – Ghardaïa – El Ménéa sur 495 km, El Ménéa et le point kilométrique 216 ainsi que Tamanrasset – Moulay Lahcen sur 213 km, soit 924 km. Ce chantier gigantesque a fait l’objet d’une réunion jeudi 1ᵉʳ octobre au siège du ministère des Travaux publics. Présidée par le ministre Abdelkader Djellaoui, elle a réuni des PDG, directeurs généraux et représentants de l'ANESRIF (Agence nationale d'études et de suivi de la réalisation des investissements ferroviaires), d'Infrarail, de Cosider TP, de Cosider OA, de la SNTP (Société nationale des travaux publics), de l'ENGOA (Entreprise nationale de réalisation d'ouvrages d'art), d'Infrafer, de Sero Est, de Sapta, des bureaux d'études Seti Rail et Saeti, et du groupe GCB, ainsi que des entreprises chinoises CRCC et CCECC, a indiqué le ministère des Travaux publics. Au menu de la réunion, « l'état de préparation des chantiers et des moyens mobilisés pour le lancement des travaux, ainsi que des mesures prises et des facilités accordées pour accompagner le projet et accélérer les démarches liées à l'aménagement des chantiers et à la mise à disposition des ressources nécessaires, garantissant ainsi le démarrage effectif des travaux dans les délais impartis », a détaillé la même source. L’article Train Alger – Tamanrasset : l’Algérie se prépare à lancer un chantier ferroviaire de 1000 km est apparu en premier sur TSA .

Ampofo Ankrah opens up on ‘constant and unrelenting’ pressure at NSA
items.description: Former National Sports Authority (NSA) Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah has spoken about the intense pressure that comes with leading the authority, describing the demands of the role as constant and unrelenting. Ampofo Ankrah was appointed Director-General by President John Dramani Mahama on March 13, 2025, succeeding Seth Panwum Boyoyo. During his tenure, Ampofo Ankrah and the NSA faced criticism over several issues, particularly the management and condition of sporting facilities across the country. Speaking to JoySports, Ampofo Ankrah acknowledged the demands of the position, stressing that the role leaves little room for excuses. “It’s different when you’re put in a position where the pressure is constant and unrelenting. There are no excuses. What I’ve noticed about the NSA is that there are no excuses,” he said. Ampofo Ankrah was asked to step aside on October 1, 2026, pending investigations into allegations surrounding a visa facilitation arrangement linked to the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The NSA has denied the allegations, while investigations into the matter continue.

items.title: Journées « Togo propre » : Les populations des Savanes mobilisées pour assainir leur environnement
items.description: Dapaong, 3 oct. (ATOP) – La journée « Togo propre », initiée par le gouvernement pour promouvoir un environnement sain, a été observée le samedi 3 octobre dans plusieurs localités de la région des Savanes, à travers des opérations de salubrité publique. L’opération au domicile du chef canton de Korbongou Ces opérations ont mobilisé les populations autour de leurs responsables locaux. Elles ont permis d’assainir plusieurs espaces publics afin d’améliorer le cadre de vie et de lutter contre les maladies liées à l’insalubrité. Dans la préfecture de Tône, les travaux se sont déroulés à la direction régionale de l’Éducation des Savanes, dans la commune Tône 1, au marché de Naki-Ouest, dans la commune Tône 2, ainsi qu’au domicile du chef canton de Korbongou, dans la commune Tône 4. Dans la préfecture de Cinkassé, les populations du canton de Nadjoundi, dans la commune Cinkassé 2, ont assaini le dispensaire de la localité. Le préfet, les autorités communales et les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) ont pris part à l’opération. Le marché de Naki ouest assaini Dans les préfectures de l’Oti et de l’Oti-Sud, les opérations ont concerné les chefs-lieux des quatre communes, notamment Mango, Barkoissi, Takpamba et Gando. Elles ont mobilisé les autorités administratives et militaires, les volontaires d’engagement citoyen (VEC), les jeunes et les femmes. À Mango, dans la commune Oti 1, les travaux ont porté sur le site de la mairie et les quartiers Djabou, Fomboro, Douane et Sangbana. Dans la commune Oti 2, les populations ont nettoyé le marché de Barkoissi, la mairie et les alentours de la poste. À Gando, dans la commune Oti-Sud 1, les travaux ont concerné les artères de la ville et le site destiné à accueillir les nouveaux locaux de la mairie. À Takpamba, dans la commune Oti-Sud 2, les populations ont assaini le site de la mairie et ses alentours, le nouveau site de la police ainsi que le marché. Togo propre à Borgou Dans la préfecture de Kpendjal, les habitants de la commune Kpendjal 1, munis de balais, de houes, de râteaux, de pelles et de brouettes, ont nettoyé le marché de Mandouri. Ils ont également entretenu la piste reliant les villages de Tambaté et de Djambotchile, dans le canton de Koundjoaré. À Borgou, dans la commune Kpendjal 2, l’opération s’est déroulée au marché à bétail. Dans la préfecture de Tandjouaré, les populations se sont mobilisées pour assainir les alentours du centre médico-social (CMS) de Bomboaka, dans la commune Tandjouaré 1. L’activité s’est déroulée en présence du secrétaire général de la préfecture, du maire de Tandjouaré 1 ainsi que des autorités civiles et militaires. Les autorités locales ont salué la mobilisation des populations et les ont invitées à maintenir cette dynamique afin de préserver un environnement sain et de prévenir les maladies liées à l’insalubrité. ATOP/JK/SED

items.title: Wike accuses Amaechi of using mother’s death for political purposes
items.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has accused former Transportation Minister Rotimi Amaechi of “descending so low” by bringing his late mother into political arguments. Wike spoke on Saturday during a visit to the Uzugbani Ekpeye National Executive Council at Ekpeye House in Ahoada East Local Government Area of Rivers State. He was reacting to Amaechi’s claim during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday: the policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration contributed to his mother’s death by making it difficult for his family to afford her medication. Wike criticised Amaechi for bringing his mother into political arguments, saying the deceased should be “resting peacefully.” “Anybody who watched television last night would cry when somebody is bringing his own mother to play politics. Your mother that we thought should be resting peacefully,” Wike said. “In one of the videos, he said if ADC wins election, his mother would be very happy,” Wike said. “So, the only condition is that your mother will not be happy if ADC does not win. Too bad! She will not be happy. But ADC will not win. How can you bring a loved one who just died to bring in politics?” Wike also questioned Amaechi’s claim that he could not afford his mother’s medication, citing his former positions as Speaker of the Rivers State House of Assembly, governor and minister. “This was a speaker for eight years, from 1999 to 2007. This was a governor for eight years, from 2007 to 2015,” he said. “This was a minister for eight years, from 2015 to 2023, and your mother was sick, and you are telling the whole world, and because of the policy of Tinubu, you couldn’t buy drugs for your mother, and so your mother died.” The FCT minister further questioned why Amaechi did not seek financial assistance from friends and associates if he could not afford the medication. “You have told the world that your wife is an industrialist, yet an industrialist couldn’t give you money to buy drugs for your mother,” Wike said. “Look at who-is-who who came with all private jets to bury a woman whom you could not buy drugs for because you were taking care of other people. You didn’t tell them, ‘My mother was sick, can you help me? Give me money; let me buy drugs.’” Wike described Amaechi’s comments as an attempt to use his mother’s death for political purposes. “People can descend so low to use their mother to play politics,” he said. He also questioned Amaechi’s claim that he could not afford his mother’s drugs, referring to properties he said the former governor owns in Old GRA, Port Harcourt, and Abuja. “Look at the house you are living in in Old GRA, look at the house you are living in in Abuja, and then you say you are unable to buy drugs, and that was why your mother died. Enough is enough of this kind of embarrassment,” Wike said. The post Wike accuses Amaechi of using mother’s death for political purposes appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 50 West African universities converge on OAU for WAUG
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo About fifty universities from the West African region have converged on the Obafemi Awolowo University OAU Ile-Ife, Osun State for the 2026 West African University Games, WAUG. Speaking during the opening ceremony held on Saturday at the OAU sports complex, President of WAUG, Mr Shaibu Tanko, said this year’s edition is special because the Games had been in comatose for a long time before its recent resurrection. He noted that the games were organised to foster collaboration and networking among universities across West Africa. “WAUG has been in a coma for a long time until recently that we tried to resurrect it. I must thank the university that is hosting it now because it has not been easy, especially regarding finances,” Tanko stated. The WAUG President, while commending the management of OAU for hosting the competition, urged “athletes to use the opportunity to collaborate and network among themselves.” In his opening remarks, the Chairman of the Local Organising Committee, Prof. Emmanuel Akinfala, said 18 sports will feature in the 10-day competition. Prof. Akinfala, who is the Deputy Vice-Chancellor, Administration, OAU, disclosed that about 50 universities from Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal and Sierra Leone have already arrived, with more expected before full commencement on Monday. “We are going to have eighteen games, and everything will be done within ten days. The games include football, volleyball, handball, badminton, chess, table tennis, lawn tennis, hockey, cricket, swimming, eSports, and squash,” he said. The Pro-Chancellor of Obafemi Awolowo University, Ambassador Adejare Bello, said the university is proud to host the 15th edition of the competition. Bello assured that OAU will deliver a memorable Games, adding that the organising committee has put a lot in place to make the participating universities enjoy the competition. “This is the 15th edition, and in the last 10 years, OAU has hosted it for the second time. The last time was in 2023 and now again in 2026,” Bello said. He stressed the importance of sports to academic life, noting that, “It is not good to walk day and night without exercising your body. It is medically recommended that if you sit in a place for one or two hours, you have to move around and stretch your legs. “It is even recommended that you take at least 10,000 steps in a day. The university encourages that, notwithstanding that we are here to learn and do research, we must be involved in exercise,” he added. Apart from the host, other universities participating in the games include Delta State University, Benson Idahosa University, Afe Babalola University, Federal University of Agriculture and Technology, Oke-Iho, Ladoke Akintola University of Technology and Lead City University. Others are: University of Ilesa, Osun State University, Plateau State University, University of Development Studies, Ghana, University of Energy and Natural Resources, Ghana, University of Ilorin, University of Ghana, University of Abuja. items.title: Égypte-Sénégal : le président Diomaye Faye ouvre de nouvelles pistes de coopération
items.description: En marge du Forum d’affaires Alamein-Afrique, le Président Bassirou Diomaye Faye a multiplié, samedi, les audiences avec des responsables économiques égyptiens. Transport aérien, formation, fret et financement des échanges ont été au cœur de ces entretiens. Le séjour du Président Bassirou Diomaye Faye en Égypte prend une tournure résolument économique. À El-Alamein, le chef de l’État a consacré, selon la communication de la présidence, une partie de son agenda à des rencontres avec des dirigeants du secteur privé et financier égyptien, avec l’objectif de renforcer les relations économiques entre Dakar et Le Caire. Parmi les principales audiences de ce samedi figure celle accordée à Hussein Sherif Fahmi, président-directeur général d’Air Cairo, deuxième compagnie aérienne d’Égypte. Les échanges ont porté sur le projet de reprise d’une liaison aérienne directe entre Le Caire et Dakar, actuellement en préparation par la compagnie égyptienne. Air Cairo veut accompagner Air Sénégal La rencontre ne s’est pas limitée à la question de la desserte aérienne. Air Cairo s’est également déclarée disposée à accompagner Air Sénégal dans la formation de ses ingénieurs, de ses mécaniciens et de son personnel navigant. La compagnie égyptienne envisage par ailleurs l’ouverture d’une ligne cargo entre l’Égypte et le Sénégal, afin de soutenir les échanges commerciaux entre les deux pays. Pour Hussein Sherif Fahmi, la position géographique du Sénégal constitue un atout, le pays pouvant servir de plateforme vers l’Afrique, l’Europe et les Amériques. Une éventuelle reprise de la liaison directe Le Caire-Dakar permettrait ainsi de renforcer les connexions entre les deux pays, tout en ouvrant des perspectives dans les domaines du transport de marchandises et de la formation aux métiers de l’aérien. De nouveaux projets éoliens et solaires au Sénégal Le Président Bassirou D. Faye a, par la suite, échangé avec Mohamed Ismail Mansour, fondateur du groupe Infinity. Déjà présent au Sénégal avec le parc éolien de Taïba Ndiaye, à travers Infinity Power, le groupe entend renforcer ses investissements avec de nouveaux projets éoliens et solaires totalisant 1 gigawatt de capacité. Ces projets devraient contribuer à accroître significativement la production nationale d’électricité et à soutenir l’objectif de souveraineté énergétique inscrit dans l’Agenda Sénégal 2050. C'est cash avec la Banque nationale d’Égypte Il y a eu une troisième audience dans la matinée : celle avec Mohamed Mahmoud El Etreby, président de la Banque nationale d’Égypte et président de l’Association des banques égyptiennes. Les discussions ont porté sur le financement des échanges entre le Sénégal et l’Égypte. Selon les informations rapportées à l’issue de cette rencontre par la présidence, la Banque nationale d’Égypte souhaite nouer un partenariat bancaire et commercial avec le Sénégal, avec notamment la perspective d’une implantation à Dakar. Une présence bancaire égyptienne dans la capitale sénégalaise pourrait fournir de nouveaux instruments aux opérateurs économiques des deux pays pour leurs transactions et contribuer au développement du commerce bilatéral. Une diplomatie économique assumée Ces audiences donnent une dimension concrète au volet économique du déplacement présidentiel. La Présidence avait annoncé, avant le départ du chef de l’État, que son séjour à El-Alamein serait consacré non seulement aux priorités du développement et de l’intégration africains, mais également à la recherche de partenariats économiques et à la présentation des opportunités offertes par le Sénégal aux investisseurs. Le passage du Président Faye à El-Alamein combine ainsi les rendez-vous institutionnels africains et les contacts directs avec des acteurs économiques. En sa qualité de président en exercice de la Cedeao, il doit également prendre part à la réunion de coordination mi-annuelle de l’Union africaine et des communautés économiques régionales. Au-delà des déclarations d’intention, les audiences de ce samedi mettent sur la table plusieurs pistes concrètes : une liaison aérienne directe Le Caire-Dakar, la formation des personnels d’Air Sénégal, une éventuelle ligne cargo, des projets éoliens et solaires, et un partenariat bancaire pouvant déboucher sur l’ouverture d’une banque égyptienne à Dakar.

items.title: Des acteurs de Saint-Louis et Louga mobilisés autour d’un projet de cuisson propre
items.description: Des acteurs des régions de Saint-Louis et de Louga se sont réunis jeudi à Saint-Louis pour une consultation autour d’un projet de cuisson propre porté par l’organisation Africa Emergence Group (AEG) en partenariat avec l'Organisation indienne Planethos. L’initiative vise à promouvoir les foyers améliorés auprès des populations vulnérables et à contribuer à la lutte contre les changements climatiques. La promotion de modes de cuisson plus propres était au cœur de l’atelier des parties prenantes organisé jeudi à Saint-Louis. La rencontre a réuni des acteurs communautaires et institutionnels des régions de Saint-Louis et de Louga, appelés à accompagner la diffusion d’un projet initié par Planethos, avec l’appui de son partenaire opérationnel au Sénégal, Africa Emergence Group (AEG). Selon le consultant Abdoul Mbaye, l’objectif est de permettre aux populations vulnérables ciblées dans les deux régions d’accéder à des foyers améliorés. « L’objectif, c’est vraiment de doter l’ensemble des habitants vulnérables et ciblés dans ces deux localités de foyers améliorés pour une cuisson propre », a-t-il expliqué. Deux modèles de foyers, dont le CV 300, ont été présentés au cours de la rencontre. Ils sont destinés à améliorer les pratiques de cuisson et à réduire la consommation de bois ainsi que les émissions de carbone. Au-delà de l’enjeu environnemental, le projet entend apporter des bénéfices sanitaires et socio-économiques aux ménages. Les foyers améliorés devraient contribuer à réduire l’exposition aux fumées, notamment les risques liés aux maladies respiratoires, tout en permettant aux femmes de gagner du temps et de réduire certaines dépenses liées à la cuisson. Abdoul Mbaye a également évoqué la sécurité des filles et des femmes qui se déplacent parfois en brousse pour chercher du bois. « C’est un gain de temps, en tout cas pour la famille. C’est un gain en économie, c’est un gain également pour le climat », a-t-il souligné. Acteur communautaire et président de conseil de quartier, Oumar Sow a salué une initiative qui favorise, selon lui, une synergie entre les communautés de Saint-Louis et de Louga. Il a estimé que l’utilisation des foyers améliorés contribuera à rendre l’environnement « plus propre et sobre en carbone », tout en réduisant l’inhalation des fumées et la pression exercée sur les forêts et la biodiversité. Représentant le maire de Saint-Louis, Mansour Faye, Lika Gueye Sarr a également salué l’initiative de Planethos et d’AEG. Elle a rappelé la vulnérabilité de Saint-Louis face aux effets des changements climatiques. « Accueillir aujourd’hui ce type de projet est bénéfique pour la communauté et pour les populations de manière générale », a-t-elle déclaré. Les acteurs communautaires présents à l’atelier ont ainsi exprimé leur engagement à accompagner la sensibilisation et l’adhésion des populations à cette nouvelle approche de cuisson. Jeanne SAGNA (Correspondante)

items.title: États-Unis : après l’exécution ratée de Christa Pike, le chef de l’administration pénitentiaire du Tennessee démissionne
items.description: Le commissaire du Departement correctionnel du Tennessee (TDOC), Frank Strada, « a presente sa demission et quittera ses fonctions ce mois-ci », a annonce ce 3 octobre le gouverneur de cet etat du Sud des etats-Unis, Bill Lee, sans directement evoquer l'execution ratee de Christa Pike. « Je suis reconnaissant a M. Strada de faire passer en premier les interets des habitants du Tennessee dans ce moment difficile », a indique Bill Lee, qui avait annonce le 1er octobre la suspension des executions au Tennessee ainsi qu'une enquete independante sur cet echec. « Je continue a penser que l'administration penitentiaire a rempli ses obligations en vertu du protocole etabli », a pour sa part precise Frank Strada, cite dans le communique. « Demissionner est toutefois dans le meilleur interet des habitants du Tennessee pendant que l'enquete independante se deroule », a ajoute le chef demissionnaire, estimant cette enquete « necessaire ». Condamnee a mort en 1996, a l'âge de 20 ans, pour le meurtre l'annee precedente - en compagnie de son petit ami et d'un troisieme complice – de Colleen Slemmer, Christa Pike devait etre executee le 30 septembre, faisant d'elle la premiere femme a subir ce sort au Tennessee en plus de deux siecles. «Le plus grand châtiment de toute l'histoire de la peine de mort aux etats-Unis» Mais Christa Pike a termine a l'hopital apres avoir survecu a deux injections de pentobarbital, un puissant anesthesiant principalement utilise - ailleurs dans le monde - pour euthanasier les animaux. « Elle est intubee, sous respirateur, et reste inconsciente», a precise son avocat, Luke Ihnen, dans une plainte deposee le 2 octobre. « Le protocole ne prevoit pas de procedures supplementaires au-dela de celles qui ont ete effectuees ce soir », avait de son cote fait le TDOC, qui a defendu la methode employee. « Apres avoir subi plus de 20 ans de detention a l'isolement et une tentative complete de la tuer par injection letale, Christa est la personne qui a subi le plus grand châtiment de toute l'histoire de la peine de mort aux etats-Unis », a fait valoir, le 1er octobre, Randy Spivey, un autre avocat de Christa Pike. « Le cas de Christa Pike met en lumiere plusieurs raisons pour lesquelles la peine de mort devrait etre abolie », a affirme le Haut-Commissaire de l'ONU aux droits de l'homme Volker Türk, dans un communique publie sur X le 1er octobre. « Les souffrances prolongees — tant physiques que psychologiques — causees par plusieurs tentatives d'execution infructueuses sont abjectes et cruelles. De plus, d'importantes questions concernant le respect du droit a un proces equitable restent sans reponse », a-t-il souligne.

items.title: Transition énergétique : Près de 4 500 pompes solaires prévues par l’Aner
items.description: Face à la flambée des coûts de l’énergie et aux pertes post-récolte, le Sénégal mise sur le solaire. Dans son plan stratégique, l’Agence nationale pour les énergies renouvelables (Aner) prévoit le déploiement de plateformes multifonctionnelles et des milliers de pompes photovoltaïques pour soutenir les activités rurales. Longtemps handicapées par l’absence ou la cherté de l’électricité, les communautés rurales trouvent aujourd’hui dans le rayonnement solaire le levier indispensable qui leur faisait défaut pour transformer durablement leur quotidien. Cette dynamique d’envergure vise avant tout l’accès direct et autonome à une énergie propre capable d’alimenter aussi bien l’irrigation des champs que la conservation des récoltes. De surcroît, cette initiative s’inscrit pleinement dans la trajectoire globale d’une Transition énergétique juste (Jetp), qui entend lier étroitement les impératifs climatiques internationaux et la justice sociale à l’échelle locale. En transformant le potentiel solaire en véritable outil de production, le pays dessine les contours d’un modèle de développement décentralisé et hautement résilient. Pendant des décennies, le manque criant d’infrastructures énergétiques modernes a agi comme un frein invisible, mais extrêmement tenace sur l’économie rurale sénégalaise. Faiblement équipés pour transformer leurs produits après la cueillette ou pour les conserver au frais, les agriculteurs ainsi que les pêcheurs voyaient une part considérable de leur labeur s’évaporer dans des pertes post-récolte inévitables. Pour les femmes qui se trouvent historiquement au centre des activités de micro-transformation et de commercialisation, l’absence de solutions modernes traduisait chaque journée en un pénible effort physique à très faible rendement économique. Une première phase expérimentale a pourtant démontré qu’une alternative solide et pérenne était parfaitement envisageable sur le terrain. Grâce à l’installation stratégique de 16 plateformes solaires multifonctionnelles réparties dans l’ensemble des 14 régions du pays, des villages autrefois totalement isolés des réseaux nationaux ont pu tester concrètement l’impact positif de ces mini centrales locales. Fort de ce succès initial particulièrement encourageant, le programme passe aujourd’hui à la vitesse supérieure pour changer d’échelle. L’objectif est de déployer 200 nouvelles plateformes solaires multifonctionnelles à travers l’ensemble du territoire national. L’irrigation solaire De plus, ces structures pensées comme de véritables hubs énergétiques communautaires intègrent désormais des chambres froides pour le stockage à basse température, des séchoirs modernes pour la valorisation des récoltes ainsi que divers équipements adaptés aux filières locales. En réduisant drastiquement le gaspillage alimentaire, l’énergie solaire devient le moteur direct de multiples activités génératrices de revenus, consolidant du même coup le tissu économique local et l’autonomie financière des femmes rurales. Parallèlement à cette valorisation indispensable hors champ, le défi majeur de la production agricole trouve quant à lui sa réponse dans l’exploitation rationnelle des nappes phréatiques. Face à la flambée constante et imprévisible des cours du gasoil, la dépendance historique aux motopompes thermiques était devenue un fardeau financier totalement insupportable pour les petites exploitations. C’est précisément pour briser ce cercle vicieux d’endettement qu’est lancé un vaste projet national de diffusion de l’irrigation photovoltaïque. Au total, ce sont 4.500 pompes solaires, réparties entre 4.000 systèmes immergés hors réseau et 500 pompes de surface, qui doivent être progressivement déployées dans les différentes zones agricoles du pays. De surcroît, pour contourner l’obstacle majeur du coût d’acquisition initial qui demeure souvent prohibitif pour les petits producteurs, un mécanisme novateur de financement mixte associant des crédits bancaires adaptés, des subventions étatiques et des paiements échelonnés a été conçu pour démocratiser à grande échelle l’accès à ces technologies de pointe. Outre la baisse significative et immédiate des charges d’exploitation pour les producteurs, ce changement majeur de paradigme promet d’assainir en profondeur l’ensemble du modèle agricole sénégalais. Il garantit en effet une meilleure gestion rationalisée de la ressource en eau, sécurise durablement les rendements face aux aléas climatiques répétés et diminue l’empreinte carbone globale du secteur primaire. De plus, avec la mise en place rigoureuse d’un système pérenne de maintenance et de formation technique des usagers, le projet crée un véritable écosystème d’emplois locaux qualifiés et non dé localisables. Pathé NIANG

items.title: Utilisation de l’énergie solaire au Sénégal : Un retard à l’allumage malgré le potentiel
items.description: Dans les vastes périmètres agricoles du Walo, chez tous, à quelques exceptions près, le pompage de l’eau se fait avec des machines à Gasoil. Ce qui coûte une fortune aux agriculteurs. Cependant, ces derniers sont aux aguets pour sauter sur des projets de pompage solaire afin de moderniser l’agriculture dans la zone. Une tendance nationale qui montre un attrait vers le solaire malgré la cherté des installations. DAGANA – Dans la zone du Walo et particulièrement, le long des berges du marigot de Niassiwu, les champs de pastèque, tomate, arachide, gombo, manioc ou oignon s’étendent sous un soleil généreux presque toute l’année. Pourtant, derrière cette image de fertilité, se cache une réalité coûteuse : le pompage de l’eau repose encore largement sur des motopompes à essence ou à gasoil. Pour des centaines d’agriculteurs du Walo, cette dépendance aux hydrocarbures grève lourdement les budgets et limite les ambitions. Beaucoup n’attendent qu’une occasion pour passer à l’énergie solaire. Parmi eux, Iba Ngom. Ce dernier est un producteur dans la zone des Trois Marigots (commune de Gandon, département de Dagana, région de Saint-Louis). Il cultive de la pastèque, de la tomate, de l’arachide et du gombo. Comme la plupart de ses collègues, il utilise le système goutte à goutte durant pratiquement toute l’année. L’eau du marigot de Niassiwu constitue sa principale source. « Nous avons installé des pompes à gasoil sur la berge. Un canal nous permet de remonter l’eau », explique-t-il. Mais l’émergence de plantes aquatiques rend l’eau plus rare et réduit la pression. Résultat : entre 5 et 10 litres de gasoil par jour selon la charge de travail. « Je suis plus qu’ouvert à me lancer dans le solaire. Je n’ai pas encore trouvé de solution pour me débarrasser du gasoil qui me vide les poches. Mais je sauterais sur la moindre occasion. Ce serait une aubaine », souligne M. Ngom. À Thila Boye, Maboye Diop, la trentaine révolue, exploite 13 hectares sur la berge du même marigot. Lui aussi pompe au gasoil. « Pour aspirer l’eau sur 200 ou 300 mètres, le coût est énorme. Si c’est l’énergie solaire, la source est là : cette zone est éclairée par le soleil presque toute l’année. Moi, je préfère les pompes solaires pour économiser mes 20 litres de gasoil quotidiens. On est vraiment prêts à passer à l’énergie solaire », assure M. Diop. Il partage les mêmes avec Souleymane Boye, agriculteur depuis 2014, qui vit uniquement de cette activité toute l’année. Sa motopompe à gasoil peut coûter plus d’un million de FCfa. Chaque semaine, il consomme environ 60 litres, hors autres frais. En plus, il emploie cinq personnes qu’il rémunère entre 600.000 et 700.000 FCfa par campagne de dix mois. « On n’a jamais attendu grand-chose de l’État, mais j’ai entendu qu’il prévoyait de promouvoir de nouveaux systèmes solaires dans l’agriculture dans le Walo. C’est un bon signe », estime S. Boye. « Cela m’arrangerait d’avoir l’énergie solaire. Le sol est fertile. Il faut juste nous encourager pour relever les défis de l’agriculture ». Autre contrainte : laisser les pompes sur la berge oblige à payer des gardiens jour et nuit. Toutefois, ces témoignages illustrent un avis partagé. Les producteurs locaux, souvent de jeunes exploitants, supportent des charges récurrentes élevées et subissent les aléas de l’approvisionnement en carburant ainsi que les difficultés liées à la raréfaction de l’eau dans certains cours d’eau. Avis partagé Cependant, les systèmes solaires restent encore l’apanage de quelques grandes entreprises installées dans la zone. Pourtant, le potentiel est évident : ensoleillement quasi permanent, besoin permanent d’irrigation, et volonté affichée de réduire les coûts pour augmenter les superficies et améliorer la rentabilité. Un exemple existe déjà à la station de pompage de Dagana. Samba Niang, responsable de cette station qui alimente les champs de plus d’une centaine de producteurs (riz, tomate, arachide, oignon), décrit une installation hybride. Avant le solaire, le coût hydraulique coûte bien plus cher à l’hectare. Avec l’apport des panneaux, il a drastiquement baissé. « Nous avons de l’eau dans toutes les zones en campagne et le rendement est acceptable. Mais la capacité reste moyenne, car nous n’avons pas beaucoup de plaques pour stocker de l’énergie. Nous attendons une réduction supplémentaire des coûts, un meilleur stockage d’énergie et la possibilité d’augmenter les superficies cultivables », relève responsable. La visite de l’Agence nationale pour les énergies renouvelables (Aner) et la présentation de projets de systèmes de pompage solaires ont suscité un réel enthousiasme. « Nous sommes ravis. Nous attendons l’arrivée de ces stations et une collaboration totale avec les bailleurs pour faciliter leur acquisition », confie Samba Niang. Passer au solaire ne se limite pas à une simple substitution technique. Pour ces agriculteurs, cela signifie alléger la facture énergétique, sécuriser l’irrigation malgré les variations du niveau d’eau, réduire la dépendance aux hydrocarbures et, à terme, rendre l’agriculture plus durable et plus compétitive. Dans un contexte où le sol reste fertile et où les cultures de contre-saison sont essentielles, l’énergie solaire apparaît comme une réponse adaptée aux contraintes du Walo. Les producteurs ne demandent pas un miracle. Ils demandent un accès facilité à des équipements solaires fiables, un accompagnement technique et des mécanismes de financement adaptés. Ils sont prêts. Le soleil, lui, est déjà là ! Il ne reste plus qu’à transformer cette disponibilité naturelle en énergie pour les champs. Par Tidiane SOW (Correspondant)

items.title: NDC’s failed 24-Hour Economy has become 24-Hour demolition – Dr. Bawumia
items.description: The 2028 presidential candidate of the New Patriotic Party, Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, has delivered a damning assessment of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) government’s two years in office, declaring that its much-touted 24-Hour Economy has become a 24-hour demolition exercise. Addressing the National Delegates Conference in Kumasi, Dr. Bawumia said the government is struggling to fulfill many of its lofty promises to Ghanaians, particularly the youth. “The NDC promised Ghanaians and the youth of this country in search of jobs a flagship 24-hour economy with one job, three shifts and 3 people (1-3-3). Nearly two years have passed and the jobs have not come or even showing any signs of coming,” Dr. Bawumia said. “The young graduate and artisan who voted for the NDC because of this sweet promise of a dramatic job boom through the 1 job 3 shifts, 3 people offer under the NDC is still waiting for his or her shift,” he said. “Sadly, the promised 24-hour economy jobs have now turned into 24-hour demolition of buildings for a so-called 24-hour markets even the NDC cannot explain,” he added. Failed promises Dr. Bawumia listed a litany of what he described as failed promises, saying the Women’s Development Bank, which was supposed to empower market women, has not opened its doors to a single woman almost two years on. He also accused the government of worsening the cost of living. According to him, instead of the promised reduction in electricity tariff under the 24-hour economy, there has been a dramatic increase, crippling households, small businesses and industries. “Today, the barber shop owner, the hair salon operator, the bread baker and many young businesses who were promised better electricity tariffs are now striving to survive because much of their sales are going into electricity bills under the NDC government,” he noted. He added that transportation, spare parts, fuel and rent costs continue to rise, arguing that even though inflation has declined to 5% on paper, the real cost of living has increased massively. Dr. Bawumia said the government’s only lifeline has been the relative stability of the Cedi, which he attributed to the NPP’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme, recalling that in June 2021, on his recommendation, the Bank of Ghana launched the programme to protect the currency from global shocks. “Records show how the programme saved our economy from serious crisis and revamp of the cedi. And the programme is today the major support behind the stability of the cedi, and with it the easing of inflation and interest rates that this government now celebrates. Ironically, key officials of the government today opposed the policy when it was introduced, vehemently claiming it was not feasible,” he said. He warned that “a good tool in careless hands becomes an expensive one,” alleging that the government is making unprecedented losses on the programme. He further accused the government of abandoning crucial NPP legacies projects like Agenda 111 district hospitals, which he said would have provided access to healthcare and jobs if completed. He also accused the NDC of making unrealistic promises to end galamsey in months and restore polluted water bodies. “Ghanaians are reminded every day of how the NDC and its senior officials, many of whom are cabinet ministers and top CEOs today, lambasted the NPP government and told Ghanaians that they possessed the magic to end galamsey instantly if voted into office. Today, under their watch, in nearly two years, galamsey has grown embarrassingly worse,” he noted. On Free SHS, he said the programme is suffering after the NDC promised to improve it. “After they promised to improve meals for students, today it has deteriorated. Many of our young BECE graduates are being deliberately cut off from Free SHS and what frustrated parents are told by the government is that their wards have deservedly failed,” he said. He reminded delegates and the nation that the NDC never believed in Free SHS and bastardised it for years until they saw its impact. On cocoa and other promises, he said: “The promises to cocoa farmers to increase the cocoa price to GH¢6,500 has turned out to be a scam. The promise of automatic posting of teachers and nurses… has turned out to be another scam. Even their much-touted ‘Nkoko nkitikiti’programme has failed.”

items.title: Aiyedatiwa assures corps members of safety
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, has assured corps members deployed to the state of a safe, peaceful and conducive environment throughout their one-year national service. Aiyedatiwa gave the assurance during the swearing-in ceremony for the 2026 Batch ‘C’ Stream I corps members deployed to Ondo State, held at Ikare-Akoko. Represented by the Commissioner for Youth and Sports Development, Segun Henry Omoyofunmi, the governor said the security and welfare of corps members remained priorities of his administration. “Let me assure you that the security and welfare of corps members remain important priorities of this administration. “The state government will continue to work closely with the NYSC and relevant security agencies to ensure that corps members serving in Ondo State enjoy a safe, peaceful and conducive environment throughout their service year,” he said. The governor urged the corps members to take full advantage of the Skills Acquisition and Entrepreneurship Development (SAED) programme, saying the skills acquired could help them become self-reliant after their service year. “The skills you acquire through this programme can become valuable tools for self-reliance, entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihoods beyond the service year. “The Ondo State Government remains committed to creating an enabling environment for young people to develop their talents, establish businesses and contribute meaningfully to the economic growth of our state,” he said. Aiyedatiwa also advised the corps members to serve with integrity and discipline while respecting the people and institutions in their host communities. He urged them to embrace diversity, build relationships across cultural and geographical boundaries, and remain committed to national unity and peaceful coexistence. “I therefore charge you to uphold the rules and regulations of the NYSC scheme and to conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of responsible Nigerian youths. “Be ambassadors of unity, agents of positive change and champions of peace wherever you find yourselves,” he added. In her address, the NYSC State Coordinator, Kuburat Omowumi Bakare, also urged the corps members to take the SAED programme seriously. She said the initiative offered practical and entrepreneurial skills that could enhance their economic independence and contribute to job creation. “This initiative offers you practical and entrepreneurial skills that can enhance your economic independence and contribute to job creation. “I urge you to take full advantage of the training opportunities available and to develop competencies that will remain relevant beyond your service year,” she said. Bakare advised the corps members to be good ambassadors of the NYSC, their families and their institutions, urging them to serve with humility, integrity and dedication. She also appreciated Governor Aiyedatiwa for his continued support for the NYSC scheme and the welfare of corps members in the state. The Chairman of the NYSC Governing Board, represented by the Permanent Secretary, Lanre Abiodun, urged the corps members to approach their service year with an open mind, a positive spirit and a determination to make meaningful contributions. He also appealed for continued cooperation among government institutions, host communities, employers, traditional institutions, security agencies and other partners to enable corps members contribute effectively wherever they are deployed. The post Aiyedatiwa assures corps members of safety appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Éthiopie: après la prise de l'aéroport, l'armée fédérale fait son entrée dans Mekele
items.description: L’armée fédérale éthiopienne est entrée aujourd’hui dans Mekele, capitale régionale du Tigré située à 150 kilomètres de la frontière érythréenne. Hier déjà, des troupes tigréennes alliées au gouvernement avaient repris l’aéroport de la ville, aux mains des rebelles du Front de libération du peuple du Tigré (TPLF) depuis le 23 septembre. C’est une prise majeure pour l’armée, qui ces derniers jours a gagné du terrain au Tigré, mais aussi plus à l’est, en Afar.

items.title: Lai Mohammed: Africa must exploit $1.3trn MICE market
items.description: By Joseph Erunke Former Minister of Information and Culture, Alhaji Lai Mohammed, has urged African governments to reposition the Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE) industry as a major economic tool, saying the continent currently accounts for only about four per cent of a global market estimated at $1.3 trillion. Mohammed said African countries could no longer afford to treat MICE mainly as a tourism activity, arguing that business events should be deliberately used to attract investment, expand trade, build partnerships and create jobs. The former minister made the call while speaking as a panellist at the ninth Africa MICE Summit in Mombasa, Kenya, themed, “Building Africa’s MICE Economies.” He said conferences and exhibitions should serve as platforms for bringing investors, buyers, policymakers, experts and businesses directly into African economies. “ MICE should not be seen simply as people coming to Africa, staying in hotels, eating in restaurants and flying home. “MICE is an economic instrument. It can bring investors, buyers, policymakers, experts and businesses into our economies. In other words, MICE can become Africa’s deal-making engine,” he said. Mohammed urged African countries to develop MICE strategies around their respective economic and cultural strengths rather than competing indiscriminately for the same events. He cited Nigeria’s entertainment industry, Kenya’s athletics and tourism sectors, South Africa’s conference industry and Rwanda’s emergence as a regional business gateway as examples of comparative advantages that could be converted into stronger MICE economies. The former minister also advocated collective African bids for major international events, with hosting responsibilities shared among countries. He cited the joint hosting of the 2026 FIFA World Cup by Canada, Mexico and the United States as an example of how countries could collaborate to stage major international events. Turn events into economic ecosystems Mohammed identified Lagos as a potential case study in transforming events into wider economic opportunities, recalling a study commissioned during his tenure as minister which indicated that about 20,000 events were held in the city every month. He also cited the growth of “Detty December” as evidence of how major events could stimulate activity across sectors including aviation, hospitality, transportation, entertainment, media, fashion, technology and retail. “The opportunity is to turn events into ecosystems,” he said. However, Mohammed, who chairs the Board of Trustees and Governing Council of the Eko Tourism Foundation, said Africa’s MICE ambitions would remain constrained without significant improvements in infrastructure and ease of movement across the continent. He listed convention centres, hotels, airports, transportation networks, digital infrastructure and reliable utilities among the facilities needed to attract major international events. He also called for improved intra-African air connectivity, wider adoption of e-visas and visa-on-arrival arrangements where appropriate, as well as expedited visa processing for accredited conference delegates. Beyond physical infrastructure, Mohammed said African countries must strengthen their broader investment environments, warning that political uncertainty, policy reversals, weak institutions and corruption could undermine investor confidence. “Africa does not only have to sell its opportunities. It has to sell credibility,” he said. Shift from delegate numbers to investment Mohammed said African governments should also change how they measure the success of business events. Rather than focusing mainly on delegate numbers and hotel occupancy, he urged governments to track investments attracted, business meetings held, trade generated and jobs created through MICE activities. He further advocated the establishment of empowered National Convention Bureaux in African countries to bid for major international events, coordinate government and private-sector efforts, facilitate business visitors, generate MICE intelligence and measure the economic impact of events. According to him, smaller African countries could also become significant MICE destinations by positioning themselves as platforms connecting businesses and markets rather than merely as destinations for consumption. He cited Rwanda’s positioning as a regional business gateway as an example of how a smaller country could leverage strategic positioning to attract business events. Mohammed said the ultimate test of any MICE event should go beyond attendance figures. “Did an investment come? Did a trade relationship begin? Did a business partnership emerge? Did jobs get created? “That is when MICE stops being merely an event, and becomes an engine of economic transformation,” he said. Delegates from 19 countries participated in the two-day summit, which was formally opened by the County Executive Council Member for Tourism, Culture and Trade, County of Mombasa, Mohamed Osman Ali. items.title: ‘If you steal from Americans, you will be jailed’ — Trump warns fraudsters
items.description: US President Donald Trump has called on Congress to introduce mandatory prison sentences for people convicted of defrauding Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security, while proposing personal financial liability for state and local politicians who knowingly fail to stop fraud. Trump made the call in a video posted on Truth Social on Saturday, saying the proposed legislation would eliminate probation as an option for people convicted of stealing from federal benefit programmes. “Today, I’m calling on Congress to pass legislation to address fraud in Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security programs,” Trump said. “First, Congress must impose mandatory minimum sentences on fraudsters who steal from critical benefit programs designed to take care of the sick, feed the hungry, care for our children, and protect our senior citizens, retirees.” He said people convicted of stealing from the programmes should face lengthy prison terms, with tougher penalties based on the amount stolen. “Under our proposal, probation is no longer an option for the fraudsters. If you steal from the American people, you will go to prison, and for a long period of time,” he said. “And the more you steal, the longer you’ll stay in that prison. Not only that, but if you’re a convicted fraudster who gets caught stealing from the American people a second time, your sentence will be doubled.” Trump also proposed doubling the sentence of convicted fraudsters who are caught committing the offence for a second time. “If you’re a convicted fraudster who gets caught stealing from the American people a second time, your sentence will be doubled,” he said. The president further proposed making state and local politicians personally liable for losses caused by fraud if they knew about it, had the power to stop it but failed to act. “Under our proposal, if a state or local politician knows about fraud and has the ability to stop it, but does nothing about it, they can be personally liable for the full loss of the American taxpayers’ money that they should have stopped and they should have saved,” Trump said. Trump did not provide specific sentencing ranges or explain in the video what legal standard would determine whether an elected official knew about fraud or had the ability to prevent it. The proposal comes amid stepped-up federal efforts by the Trump administration to combat fraud involving government benefit programmes. “This legislative proposal will make fraudsters think long and hard before they keep stealing from the American people and will make crooked and corrupt politicians think also long and hard before they ignore fraud that they can stop and that they should stop,” Trump said. He ended the video with a warning: “So from now on, fraudsters, we’re watching you.” The post ‘If you steal from Americans, you will be jailed’ — Trump warns fraudsters appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Stampede at NPP conference leaves three injured in Kumasi
items.description: At least three people have sustained injuries after a stampede broke out among crowds attending the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) National Delegates Conference at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi. The affected individuals were taken to the Kumasi South Hospital for medical attention, while others who suffered minor injuries received treatment at temporary medical points established within the conference grounds. One of the injured persons is reported to have suffered a fracture when some people attempted to push their way through the crowd. The incident prompted police officers at the venue to step up crowd control efforts and prevent further congestion around the affected area. The large turnout also created difficulties for emergency responders, with personnel from the Ghana National Ambulance Service reportedly struggling to move through the crowd to reach and evacuate the injured. The incident occurred as delegates and supporters gathered for the NPP’s national executive elections.

items.title: 2027 Polls: CSOs demand stringent action against vote-buying
items.description: …as FG okays quarterly policy dialogue By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) on Friday identified vote-buying as a major problem that the Federal Government must find ways to tackle ahead of the 2027 general elections. In separate presentations at the 2026 National CSOs Summit held in Abuja, representatives of various organisations working to promote credible, transparent and inclusive elections in the country decried the repeated failure to prosecute individuals previously arrested for vote-buying. They said the country’s electoral process would continue to be undermined unless stringent measures were adopted to ensure the prosecution and conviction of offenders, thereby serving as a deterrent to others. In his remarks, the Executive Director of the Value Rebirth and Empowerment Initiative (VREI), Pastor Edewor Egedegbe, argued that a credible and peaceful election requires informed citizens. He maintained that reports of inadequate funding for the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) “raise serious concerns about preparations for the election, which is just months away.” He added that late funding not only disrupts the planning process but also increases the risk of avoidable failures. Insisting that the electoral body had not done much in terms of voter enlightenment, Egedegbe said INEC must also open its books by publishing what it has received so far. “It should start procurement of needed items and embark on the training of essential manpower. “Democracy succeeds where citizens participate in the process without fear or intimidation,” he added. For his part, the Executive Director of the Peering Advocacy and Advancement Center in Africa (PAACA), Chief Ezenwa Nwagwu, highlighted the importance of encouraging citizens to register and obtain the Permanent Voters Card (PVC), which he said carries more value than a bank Automated Teller Machine (ATM) card. “This is what we should be emphasising. The cost of electricity is embedded in the PVC, so also is the cost of education and everything about life in the country. “It is not about asking people to take money from candidates and vote their conscience. When you sell your PVC, it diminishes your citizenship. “The fact that you think the law does not work in the country does not mean that you cannot be used as an example to show how the law works,” Nwagwu stated. He blamed the recurring cases of vote-buying during elections on what he described as “the pauperisation of citizens.” “Until we realise the powers we have as citizens, we will continue to shortchange ourselves. “We should always ask ourselves this question: if votes don’t count, why then do politicians place value on your votes? “As we move towards the 2027 general elections, we as citizens have to re-examine ourselves and take over the power of polling units from the politicians. The citizens must drive the process,” he insisted. Meanwhile, the federal government said it had approved the establishment of a quarterly civil society policy dialogue forum to institutionalise citizens’ participation in policy formulation, implementation and evaluation. The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, who represented President Bola Tinubu at the summit, said the forum would provide a structured platform for evidence-based advocacy and ensure that community-level concerns were reflected in government decisions. He also pledged the FG’s commitment to expand civic space for social accountability, including greater collaboration with accredited CSOs on public finance transparency, budget tracking and monitoring of humanitarian and grassroots interventions. “This administration firmly believes that no nation can achieve inclusive, equitable and sustainable development without a vibrant, credible and responsible civil society operating within an open and enabling civic space,” he added. The National Convener of the CSOs Summit, Ambassador Kunle Yusuff, who is the Director-General of the Civil Society Organisations on Community Advancement and Humanitarian Empowerment Initiative (CSCHEI), said the aim was to galvanise the various organisations to brainstorm on the way forward as the nation braces for another round of elections. Yusuff said the summit was proposing a sustainable partnership compact through which the government, civil society and the private sector could work jointly on national priorities rather than operating from positions of suspicion. According to him, the proposed framework will provide a mechanism for monitoring government policies, budgets and electoral promises, while ensuring that information generated from communities reaches relevant authorities. The post 2027 Polls: CSOs demand stringent action against vote-buying appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Use power to serve Ghanaians, not to intimidate – Okoe Boye to NDC
items.description: Former Health Minister Dr Bernard Okoe Boye has urged the National Democratic Congress (NDC) government to use political power to improve the lives of Ghanaians rather than to demonstrate its authority or intimidate citizens. His comments come amid public discussions surrounding the arrest of nurse Salomey Awitey Baffoe, and broader concerns over the exercise of state power. Speaking to JoyNews on Saturday, October 3, Dr Okoe Boye reminded politicians that political power is not permanent and ultimately belongs to the people who give governments the mandate to govern. He said politicians should therefore remain humble and remember that their authority is derived from ordinary Ghanaians. “You can’t stay in power for long because real power is with the man and the woman who is down,” he said. According to the former Health Minister, political parties do not inherently possess power but receive it from the electorate through the democratic process. “The NDC didn’t have power; Ghanaians gave them power,” Dr Okoe Boye said. He consequently advised politicians in government to focus less on demonstrating where power lies and more on showing citizens what that power can achieve for them. “So I would advise them: Let’s be humble as politicians. Don’t show people where power lies; show them what power can be used for,” he said. Dr Okoe Boye said political authority could be used to create jobs and provide employment opportunities for citizens. He also cited infrastructure and education as areas where government could deploy its authority and resources to make a meaningful difference in people’s lives. “You can use power to create jobs. You can use power to give people employment. You can use power to build buildings. You can use power to educate. You can use power to build scholarships,” he said. The former minister stressed that the ultimate purpose of political power should be to develop and empower citizens. “Let’s use power to build our people, not to show them where power lies,” he added. Salomey Baffoe, 40, was arrested during a midnight raid on Sunday, September 13, at her home in Hansua in the Techiman Municipality of the Bono East Region. The High Court on Thursday, September 24, denied a bail application filed on her behalf after the prosecution argued that she was still needed to assist with ongoing investigations. The court was told that the investigation was cyber-related and that her release at that stage posed a risk of interference with witnesses. The court subsequently directed the Republic to expedite its investigations.

items.title: “I’ll have no honour if your arrears are not paid by October 30,” Haruna Iddrisu tells teachers
items.description: Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu has renewed his appeal to teacher unions to call off their ongoing strike, assuring teachers that government is committed to resolving their concerns, particularly issues surrounding promotion arrears. Speaking at the 2026 Ghana Teacher Prize celebrations, Mr. Iddrisu said government was intensifying engagements with the unions to find lasting solutions to the challenges facing teachers. He gave a firm assurance that outstanding promotion arrears would be addressed, stressing that teachers deserved to be treated with dignity and respect. “If by October 30, 2026, your promotion arrears are not paid, then I will have no honour,” Haruna Iddrisu said. The Minister’s comments come as the National Teaching Council hosts the 2026 Ghana Teacher Prize under the theme “Empowering Teachers: Architects of the Future.” The two-day event, being held from October 3 to 4 at the GNAT Hall in Accra, is aimed at recognising and celebrating teachers for their contribution to education and national development. The celebrations will culminate in a grand durbar at the UPSA Auditorium on Monday, where outstanding teachers are expected to be honoured. Organisers say teachers go beyond the delivery of lessons in classrooms. They play a critical role in shaping the values, skills and knowledge that form the foundation of Ghana’s future. The theme for this year’s celebration therefore highlights the need to empower teachers with the resources, recognition and respect necessary for them to innovate, adapt and sustain their passion for the profession. It also underscores the shared responsibility of government, industry, communities and families to create an environment that enables teachers to effectively prepare young people for the future. The Registrar of the National Teaching Council, Dr. Christian Addai-Poku, said teachers must be celebrated for the critical role they play in shaping the next generation. “Teachers must be celebrated because they are the architects of the future.” As government continues its engagements with teacher unions over their concerns, the Ghana Teacher Prize provides an opportunity to recognise the dedication of teachers and reaffirm the importance of investing in the people responsible for educating the country’s future leaders. For Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu, the message is clear: “We all owe it to the teacher.”

items.title: Netanyahu invites ‘true hero’ Indian flydubai captain to Israel
items.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday invited to Israel as a guest of honour the Indian captain of a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight who offered a dramatic account of how he saved the plane after being attacked. Netanyahu said he wanted Captain Smit Machchhar and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, one of Israel’s key international partners, to light a flame at a national ceremony for Israel’s Independence Day next May, saying the role was usually reserved for Israeli citizens. “You are a true hero of the brave peoples of India and Israel and you are a hero of the entire world,” Netanyahu said in a video his office released of his telephone conversation with the hospitalised captain. UAE investigators have said that the co-pilot planned the “terrorist act” by attacking Machchhar with an axe. Asked how the attack unfolded, Machchhar said the co-pilot had asked to take time to pray, as devout Muslims do five times a day. “A lot of locals, they do pray, which is not out of the ordinary. While he was praying, out of respect, I was just looking at the front and not at the back,” Machchhar said. “Suddenly after I think I would say about four to five minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head. My first thought was that there was catastrophic damage to the aircraft and something is not right. “But then after that the blows kept coming one after the other. That’s when I realised that it’s not the aircraft, it’s the other guy who was in the cockpit with me.” While saying his memory was not entirely clear due to his injury, Machchhar said he managed to pull open the cockpit door “but I think he shut it back closed.” “I had that one last fight left in me,” Machchhar explained, saying he knew he faced certain death if not. “That’s when I pushed against everything. I gave everything that I had and just went for the door and opened the door and thankfully people were waiting.” AFP The post Netanyahu invites ‘true hero’ Indian flydubai captain to Israel appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: À Paris, “Idi Amin“ appelle au respect des libertés de chacun : « Pour m’intimider, il faut sortir peut-être l’arme nucléaire »
items.description: À l’occasion de la célébration du 68e anniversaire de l’indépendance de la Guinée en région parisienne, dans la commune de Noisy-le-Sec, l’ambassadeur de Guinée en France a livré un message de rassemblement et de fermeté. En présence de l’ancien président de la transition guinéenne, le général Sékouba Konaté, Aboubacar Sidiki Camara, dit « Idi Amin », a notamment invité ses compatriotes au respect des lois et des libertés de chacun. « La démocratie, c’est l’expression de la pluralité des opinions. Mais la liberté des uns commence là où s’arrête celle des autres. Tu es libre de dire et de penser ce que tu veux, mais tu ne peux pas imposer cela aux autres. Enfin, je vais dire que j’ai été formé dans ce pays [France]. Je ne voulais pas parler de mon cursus, mais j’ai passé dix années ici, de l’Académie de Saint-Cyr à l’École de guerre. Alors, pour m’intimider, il faut sortir peut-être l’arme nucléaire. (…) », a déclaré le diplomate guinéen dans une vidéo publiée par GuineeWeb. Ancien ministre de la Défense nationale, Aboubacar Sidiki Camara « Idi Amin » a été nommé ambassadeur extraordinaire et plénipotentiaire de la République de Guinée auprès de la France en juin 2026. Ousmane CAMARA L’article À Paris, “Idi Amin“ appelle au respect des libertés de chacun : « Pour m’intimider, il faut sortir peut-être l’arme nucléaire » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: NPP Delegates Congress: The 14 approved constitutional amendments
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has approved 14 amendments to its constitution at its National Delegates Conference in Kumasi, as the party seeks to strengthen its internal structures, administration and electoral preparedness. The amendments, proposed by the party’s Constitutional Amendments Committee, were presented to delegates for consideration and subsequently adopted through a series of voice votes. The changes cover various aspects of the party’s internal organisation, leadership and administration, with the broader objective of improving the NPP’s structures and readiness for future electoral activities. The amendments were approved as part of proceedings at the National Delegates Conference, which is also being used to elect the party’s national executives. 1. Increase representation of Council of Elders on Disciplinary Committee: Amend Articles 4(17)(c) and 16(9) to increase the representation of the National Council of Elders on the National Disciplinary Committee from one to two members. The proposal is intended to bring greater experience, wisdom and institutional perspective to disciplinary proceedings while promoting balance, fairness and confidence in the party’s disciplinary processes. 2. Additional Constituency Vice Chairperson: Amend Article 7(2) to provide for the appointment of an additional constituency vice chairperson to the Constituency Executive Committee. The proposal seeks to broaden leadership participation, facilitate the distribution of responsibilities, and improve coordination and administration at the constituency level. 3. IT Officers on executive committees : Amend Articles 7(2) and 9(1) to include Regional and Constituency Information Technology Officers as members of their respective executive committees. The amendment is intended to strengthen data management, digital coordination, accountability and information security, while giving IT officers the authority and institutional protection required to perform their technical responsibilities. 4. Deputy Communications Officers : Provide for Deputy Regional Communications Officers and Deputy Constituency Communications Officers to serve as members of their respective executive committees. The proposal follows the transition of Regional and Constituency Communications Officers from appointed to elected positions and seeks to strengthen coordination within the party’s expanding communications network. 5. Additional Regional Vice Chairpersons: Provide for two additional Regional Vice Chairpersons on Regional Executive Committees to broaden leadership participation, facilitate the distribution of responsibilities and improve coordination and administration at the regional level. 6. Voting rights for Regional Council of Elders chairpersons: Amend Article 10(13) to grant chairpersons of Regional Councils of Elders voting rights at the National Delegates Conference. The proposal seeks to ensure consistency in the allocation of voting rights, particularly as members of Regional Steering Committees already enjoy voting rights under Article 9. 7. Voting rights for Regional Patrons : Amend Article 10(13) to grant chairpersons of Regional Patrons voting rights at the National Delegates Conference. The proposal recognises the financial and other contributions of party patrons and seeks to enhance their participation in the party’s decision-making processes. 8. Administrative manual for party officers : Amend Article 10(2) to mandate the National Council to provide an administrative manual outlining the duties, responsibilities and functions of all elected and non-elected party officers at all levels. The manual is intended to promote clarity, consistency and accountability, reduce duplication and conflicts in roles, and provide officers with clear guidance in the discharge of their functions. 9. Presidential candidate to lead campaign structure: Amend Articles 10(3), 10(3)(2) and 10(4)(2) to provide that the presidential candidate, in consultation with the National Executive Committee, shall develop the campaign structure for the presidential election and appoint the chairperson and other members of the National Campaign Advisory Committee, subject to approval by the National Council. The proposal seeks to align campaign leadership with the vision of the presidential candidate while maintaining institutional oversight. 10. Clarification of party leadership : Amend Articles 10(41) and 13 to provide that when the party has an elected presidential candidate, the presidential candidate shall be the leader of the party. When the party is in government, the President shall be the leader of the party until a presidential candidate is elected. The proposal seeks to formalise the party’s leadership structure and eliminate ambiguity over political leadership. 11. Three additional National Vice Chairpersons: Amend Article 10(5) to provide for three additional National Vice Chairpersons, bringing the total to six—three elected and three appointed. The appointed vice chairpersons will not be eligible for succession to the National Chairmanship. The proposal is intended to ease the workload of the National Chairman, improve regional mobilisation and promote geographical, ethnic, religious and gender balance in the party’s leadership. 12. Separate elections for National Vice Chairpersons : Amend Article 10(5) to provide that the offices of First, Second and Third National Vice Chairpersons will be separate elective positions, with each contested independently at the National Delegates Conference. Candidates will be required to indicate the specific office they intend to contest at the nomination stage. 13. President on National Steering Committee : Amend Article 10(10)(2) to reinstate the President, when the party is in government, as a member of the National Steering Committee. The amendment seeks to facilitate coordination between the party and government and enable timely consultation on political and governance matters. 14. Women’s Wing and gender participation: Amend Article 15(12) by adding a new paragraph mandating the Women’s Wing to champion and promote the progressive advancement of women’s participation in politics in accordance with the Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Act, 2024 (Act 1121). The proposal gives the Women’s Wing an institutional responsibility to promote, monitor and support increased participation of women in the party and political leadership. All 14 amendments were put to delegates for approval and were subsequently approved.

items.title: Peru, already home to over 290 lizard species, finds a new one
items.description: Scientists have discovered a new species of lizard in the Peruvian Andes, the Natural History Museum of San Marcos University said on Saturday. The lizard measures between six and eight centimetres and has distinct colouration depending on sex. Females have square-shaped spots on their backs, while males have oblique spots and white scales that help them blend into their rocky surroundings. The lizard feeds on plants and small arthropods, including spiders, beetles, true bugs and insect larvae. The new species was found at an altitude of more than 4,800 metres in the southern Andean region of Arequipa and was given the name Liolaemus archipensis . “The description of a new species represents a very important advance for biodiversity in our country,” biologist Ling Huamani-Valderrama, who led the research, told AFP . Peru is home to 296 species of lizard, according to the biologist. The discovery was published in the Swiss scientific journal Diversity . An “amphibious mouse” with partially webbed feet that eats aquatic insects was among 27 new species discovered during a 2022 expedition to Peru’s Amazon, according to Conservation International. Scientists also discovered a spiny mouse, a squirrel, eight types of fish, three amphibians and 10 types of butterflies, according to Trond Larsen, head of Conservation International’s Rapid Assessment Programme. He added that another 48 species found by investigators were potentially new, but needed further study. In July 2025, palaeontologists in Peru’s Ocucaje Desert unveiled the fossilised skeleton of an ancient, dolphin-like creature estimated to be between 8 and 12 million years old.
