items.title: Ibrahima Niakh, un acteur de développement au service du social
items.description: De retour d’Europe, Ibrahima Niakh multiplie les contributions au profit du développement de Diarrère, son village natal. Ancien membre de la Croix-Rouge locale de Moncalieri en Italie, M. Niakh a décidé de rentrer au bercail en 2014. Depuis, il s’est lancé dans la vente de charbon de bois, une activité qui l’a d’ailleurs rendu célèbre dans son fief. En plus, celui que l’on surnomme « Nar Sidy » s’investit dans le social en mettant en place des structures commerciales de proximité, comme une buvette scolaire. FATICK – Dans son Diarrère natal (région de Fatick), il marche la tête haute, car il contribue activement au développement de sa communauté. Ibrahima Niakh est un citoyen modèle, une personne dont les qualités humaines sonnent comme un refrain chez les siens. Le 9 mars 1979, la commune de Diarrère voit naître l’un de ses fils les plus entreprenants. « Nar Sidy », comme l’appellent affectueusement ses concitoyens, a réussi à écrire une belle page de l’histoire de cette localité située à quelques kilomètres de la ville de Fatick. Travailleur acharné, Niakh étend son influence grâce à de modestes investissements, à caractère social pour la plupart. Son histoire inspirante cache toute une leçon de vie. Il y a douze ans, « Nar Sidy » rentrait définitivement d’Europe. Aujourd’hui, il est, comme le veut le jargon commun, un « émigré de retour ». Bien qu’il soit de taille relativement petite, Ibrahima Niakh est une grande figure en matière d’entrepreneuriat local. À une quinzaine de mètres de la place publique de Diarrère, il tient un modeste magasin abritant des sacs remplis de charbon de bois. Depuis quelques années, il s’est lancé dans la vente de ce produit qu’il considère comme de « l’or noir ». D’une humilité exemplaire, M. Niakh a lancé ce commerce dans des conditions loin d’être évidentes. Sans instruction scolaire, le citoyen modèle de Diarrère a pourtant frappé un grand coup en réussissant à propulser son activité. Depuis son retour dans sa terre natale, il ne cesse d’approvisionner la population de son village en combustible. Le complexe d’infériorité n’a pas pu l’affaiblir ni le conditionner. D’ailleurs, il se rappelle avec fierté ses premiers pas dans une activité qui, auparavant, était jugée dévalorisante aux yeux des habitants. « Le jour où j’ai commencé à écraser et à mettre le charbon dans des sachets, beaucoup ne m’ont pas reconnu. C’était impensable pour les gens, sachant que je gagnais bien ma vie en Europe avant mon retour. Même ma femme n’y croyait pas ses yeux », se souvient-il dans un large sourire. Le parcours d’un guerrier Comme certains enfants de son âge, Ibrahima Niakh a été très tôt initié aux travaux champêtres et à l’élevage. C’est, pour ainsi dire, un pur produit du monde rural malgré un bref passage à l’école arabe. Bien avant son voyage en Italie, il avait déjà appris un métier, au-delà de faire paître le bétail ou de cultiver la terre. « J’ai appris le métier de vulcanisateur, contrairement à mes frères et sœurs qui ont usé les bancs de l’école », confie-t-il. Cependant, le jeune Niakh finit par abandonner son métier de prédilection pour se rendre hors du pays. Ainsi, le 25 juin 1996, le villageois décolle pour l’Espagne après en avoir parlé à ses grands-parents. Une fois en terre espagnole, il ne trouve rien d’autre que la cueillette de fruits, un travail loin de l’enchanter. Après seulement neuf mois, M. Niakh quitte l’Espagne pour Pau, en France, pour un séjour beaucoup plus bref. Il n’y passe que quelque temps avant de prendre le chemin de l’Italie où il s’installe à Moncalieri, une localité située à proximité de Turin. Ironie du sort, il se retrouve encore dans les champs. « J’ai finalement accepté ce que j’avais refusé en Espagne : travailler dans les plantations. Sauf qu’en Italie, c’était moins pénible et plus rentable », souffle-t-il d’un ton humoristique. C’est avec beaucoup de passion et de spontanéité que « Nar Sidy » évoque son aventure italienne, qui constitue l’épisode le plus marquant de son séjour européen. Il lui faudra attendre deux longues années avant que d’autres opportunités ne s’ouvrent à lui. Ainsi, après le métier d’ouvrier agricole, il s’investit dans la métallurgie et la mécanique pendant plusieurs années. En bon curieux, il s’adapte vite à l’environnement de sa terre d’accueil. La preuve : il réussit à intégrer la Croix-Rouge locale de Moncalieri. Un véritable exploit, puisqu’il est le premier Africain à faire partie de ce corps dans la commune. Cerise sur le gâteau, le prestigieux quotidien national italien La Stampa a rédigé un article sur lui, évoquant une ambulance offerte par les autorités locales italiennes et destinée à la population de Diarrère. Un article qu’il conserve précieusement jusqu’à ce jour. « J’ai travaillé à la Croix-Rouge de Moncalieri de 1998 à 2014, année de mon retour au Sénégal. C’était une fierté pour les autorités locales italiennes. En tant que secouriste, j’ai assisté à plusieurs matchs de Serie A et de Ligue des champions. Je garde avec moi des photos prises avec des stars comme Lilian Thuram, Cannavaro, Del Piero, Ibrahimovic… », révèle-t-il. Il a également vécu d’autres expériences marquantes avec la Croix-Rouge, notamment la couverture de catastrophes naturelles. « J’ai couvert des inondations et même un tremblement de terre survenu à Pérouse vers les années 2000-2001 », souffle-t-il. Son passage à la Croix-Rouge de Moncalieri aura été d’une grande utilité pour les siens. En 2012, il dote sa terre natale d’une ambulance offerte en Italie. Les témoignages du chef du village de Diarrère en disent long sur les valeurs de l’homme : « C’est une personne très utile qui mérite des prières. Il s’est beaucoup battu pour le bien du village. L’ambulance qu’il a amenée reste un cadeau inoubliable, car elle a énormément aidé la population. On se souvient aussi que pendant la Covid-19, Ibrahima s’est sacrifié pour protéger la population en faisant preuve d’une grande rigueur dans la sécurisation du village. Il veillait sans relâche à l’hygiène et à la sécurité des habitants », fait savoir Diène Diouf, par ailleurs président des chefs de village de la commune de Diarrère. Un symbole de confiance en soi À la porte de sa modeste entreprise, des centaines de sachets de charbon jonchent le sol. Vendus à 100 FCfa l’unité, ce sont presque des cadeaux proposés aux clients qui viennent s’approvisionner tout au long de la journée. En ce début de matinée, l’homme porte un léger short cargo, la casquette minutieusement vissée sur la tête. Au premier contact, M. Niakh dégage une apparence très simple. Pourtant, derrière cette image se cachent une vraie réussite sociale et une vie épanouie. « Il n’y a pas de sot métier » : un adage bien ancré chez ce citoyen modèle. Doté d’un mental de fer, il a su braver le jugement de la société pour monter son commerce de charbon, une ressource qu’il fait venir de régions comme Tambacounda, Kolda ou Koumpentoum. « Quand j’ai appris à ma mère que je devais me lancer dans la vente de charbon, elle l’a pris pour une blague. Les gens n’y croyaient pas. Mais, sachant ce dont je suis capable, j’ai pesé le pour et le contre, fait une étude de marché, puis je me suis lancé », explique-t-il avec passion. Sa réputation d’homme au grand cœur se confirme dans ses propos : « Je crois au commerce social. Je fais tout cela pour que les gens puissent acheter à bon prix. Avant l’aspect financier, je mise d’abord sur l’esprit d’entraide. » Au-delà du commerçant, Ibrahima Niakh est un modèle de réussite dans un contexte souvent marqué par la migration irrégulière. Selon lui, la vente de charbon génère des revenus très intéressants : « Elle est très rentable. Je la conseille vivement aux jeunes. On peut rester ici et réussir », affirme-t-il. En modèle accompli, Ibrahima ne s’est pas limité à son seul commerce. Il est l’initiateur de nombreux évènements sociaux dans sa localité. En 2016, il a lancé la « Fête du bébé de l’année », célébrant le premier nouveau-né du Nouvel An à Diarrère – une occasion d’offrir des cadeaux, des vivres et des vêtements à la mère. La célébration en est cette année à sa onzième édition. Mais Ibrahima Niakh ne compte pas s’arrêter en si bon chemin. En plus du charbon, il s’est lancé dans la vente d’eau et a créé une buvette scolaire de proximité, construite après concertation avec le chef d’établissement. Une initiative au grand bénéfice des élèves et à moindre coût, chaleureusement saluée par les villageois. « Des parents me remercient pour cette initiative. La buvette soulage les familles démunies et évite aux élèves de longs déplacements. Avant, ils devaient parcourir environ un kilomètre pendant les récréations pour se ravitailler », explique-t-il. Fort de ses riches expériences acquises en Europe, Ibrahima Niakh ambitionne désormais de mettre son savoir-faire de secouriste au service de Diarrère en y installant une antenne locale permanente de la Croix-Rouge. Par Fodé SARR (Correspondant)

items.title: IGP deploys DIG, CPs to Imo for rescue of kidnapped corps members, others
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu, has deployed the Deputy Inspector-General of Police in charge of Operations, DIG Shehu Nadada, to Imo State to coordinate the rescue of the prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and other passengers abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway on Thursday, 1 October 2026. Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete *niedu made this known in a statement on Saturday in Abuja The statement said the DIG arrived in Imo State with two Commissioners of Police and conducted an on-the-spot assessment of the situation and the ongoing search-and-rescue efforts. It added that the DIG also reviewed the operational strategies, deployment of personnel as well as operational assets, and provided further directives to strengthen the coordinated response. The statement further explained that the assessment was conducted alongside the Imo State Commissioner of Police, Audu Bosso; the Commissioner of Police, Federal Operations, Akpan Anifiok; the Commissioner of Police in charge of the Police Mobile Force; as well as other Service Commanders and members of the Management Team of the Imo State Police Command. It pointed out that the search-and-rescue operation had been further intensified, with additional deployments of tactical teams and operational assets across identified areas, backed by intelligence-led tracking of the suspects. The statement added that “the Police are working in close coordination with sister security agencies to ensure the safe rescue of the abducted persons and the apprehension of the perpetrators. “The DIG Operations, DIG Shehu Umar Nadada, assured members of the public that the Nigeria Police Force is committed to securing the safe rescue of the 20 abducted persons and will sustain the operation until the mission is successfully concluded. “He urged members of the public and the media to remain calm and vigilant and encouraged anyone with credible information that could assist the operation to promptly contact the Police or the nearest security formation.” The statement assured that “all information received will be treated with strict confidentiality and further updates will be issued as the operation progresses.” The post IGP deploys DIG, CPs to Imo for rescue of kidnapped corps members, others appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Développement: lancement du Cadre de Partenariat Pays 2026-2031 entre le Burkina Faso et la Banque mondiale
items.description: La ministre burkinabè Déléguée chargée du Budget, Fatoumata Bako/Traoré, représentant le ministre de l'Economie et des Finances, a lancé, le vendredi 2 octobre 2026, le Cadre de Partenariat Pays (CPP) 2026-2031 entre le Burkina Faso et la Banque mondiale, lors d’une cérémonie, à Ouagadougou. Le CPP 2026-2031 « n’appartient pas à la seule Banque mondiale. Il n’a pas été préparé dans les bureaux de Washington et même dans nos bureaux à Ouagadougou. Il a été le fruit de consultations régulières avec l’ensemble des forces vives du pays », a déclaré Ousmane Diagana, Vice-Président de la Banque mondiale pour l'Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre. Les membres du gouvernement burkinabè et des partenaires techniques et financiers, ont procédé, dans la soirée du vendredi 2 octobre 2026, au cours d’une cérémonie, au lancement officiel du Cadre de Partenariat Pays (CPP) entre le Groupe de la Banque mondiale et le Burkina Faso pour la période 2026-2031. Présidée par la représentante du ministre de l’Economie et des Finances, Fatoumata Bako/Traoré, ministre Déléguée chargée du Budget, qui avait à ses côtés des dirigeants de l’institution bancaire mondiale dont le Vice-Président de la Banque mondiale pour l'Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre, Ousmane Diagana, cette rencontre dépasse le cadre d'une simple cérémonie institutionnelle. Le Vice-Président de la Banque mondiale pour l'Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre, Ousmane Diagana « Il (le CPP) incarne le renouvellement d'un engagement nourri par plus de 63 années de partenariat. Oui, c'est le 3 mai 1963 que le Burkina Faso a adhéré à la Banque mondiale, et depuis lors, notre relation s'est solidement ancrée dans la confiance, le respect mutuel et une ambition partagée : celle de bâtir un Burkina Faso plus prospère, plus résilient et plus équitable pour tous ses citoyens, en particulier pour sa jeunesse », a soutenu M. Diagana. Il a, notamment, invité le gouvernement burkinabè à considérer ce qu’il a accompli avec son institution, « non comme un simple bilan administratif, mais comme la démonstration concrète que le partenariat, lorsqu'il est fondé sur la confiance et un engagement partagé, peut changer durablement la vie des populations ». Selon lui, le Cadre de Partenariat Pays 2018-2024 qui a précédé celui lancé, le vendredi 2 octobre 2026, a été mis en œuvre dans un contexte particulièrement difficile, marqué par des défis sécuritaires et humanitaires, des crises mondiales successives et de fortes contraintes opérationnelles. « Et pourtant, les résultats qui ont été accomplis sont impressionnants », a-t-il salué, précisant que le thème du lancement officiel du CPP 2026-2031, reflétant pleinement leur ambition commune, est intitulé: « Consolider les acquis, promouvoir la croissance et favoriser la création d’emplois pour la jeunesse ». Photo des familles des officiels composés notamment des membres du gouvernement et des équipes de la Banque mondiale Le CPP 2026-2031 interviendra dans plusieurs domaines de développement. Le vice-président de la Banque mondiale pour l'Afrique de l'Ouest et du Centre, Ousmane Diagana, a fait noter qu’il est le fruit d'un processus rigoureux, itératif et participatif qui s’appuie sur une évaluation objective du Cadre précédent, sur le Diagnostic Systématique Pays et surtout, sur un dialogue approfondi avec le Gouvernement burkinabè, les partenaires au développement, le secteur privé et la société civile. Ce cadre s'articule autour de quatre axes complémentaires, a poursuivi M. Diagana, ajoutant qu’il est conçu non comme une liste de projets, mais comme une vision cohérente et intégrée du développement. Il prend en compte le capital humain, l'amélioration de la productivité agricole, l'amélioration de l'accès à l'énergie et aux services financiers et le renforcement des services de base dans les villes et les communautés les plus vulnérables, notamment en matière de connectivité, de transports, d'infrastructures à faibles émissions de carbone et de protection contre les inondations. Le Vice-Président de la Banque mondiale pour l'Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre s’est attardé sur les acquis du Cadre précédent. « Dans le domaine de l'énergie, le nombre de personnes ayant accès à l'électricité est passé de 3,4 millions à plus de 28,4 millions aujourd’hui, une multiplication par vingt. Plus de 430 000 élèves déplacés par les crises ont été réintégrés dans le système scolaire. Environ 850 000 personnes ont désormais accès à l'eau potable. Soixante-dix-sept postes de santé avancés ont été déployés dans les zones les plus fragiles du pays. Enfin, la campagne agropastorale 2025-2026 a enregistré une production céréalière de plus de 7 millions de tonnes, un niveau excédentaire historique qui couvre 126% des besoins nationaux », a-t-il égrené. Il a souligné que ces performances ne sont pas celles de la Banque mondiale. « Ce sont des performances propres au gouvernement burkinabè. La Banque y a contribué que modestement avec l’accompagnement technique, financier et bien-sûr avec des conseils par un staff engagé et compétent, vivant ici au Burkina Faso », a soutenu Ousmane Diagana, enchaînant que « la croissance économique a atteint environ 5% en 2025, contre 4,8 % l'année précédente. Ces progrès sont le reflet d'une nation résiliente et qui prend en charge son destin ». Les membres du gouvernement sur la première ligne de l'aile droite En somme, pour M. Diagana, ces résultats témoignent non seulement de la qualité de leur partenariat, mais surtout de la résilience extraordinaire du peuple burkinabè face à l'adversité. Selon lui, parallèlement, le portefeuille de la Banque mondiale a poursuivi sa croissance au Burkina Faso, « passant de 2,7 milliards de dollars en 2020 à près de 4 milliards de dollars en 2025, soit donc plus de 2 400 milliards F CFA avec 29 projets actifs couvrant des secteurs-clés du développement, de l’éducation, de la santé, de l’agriculture, de l’élevage, de l’énergie, etc ». Pour Ousmane Diagana, la Banque mondiale est pleinement consciente des défis considérables auxquels le Burkina Faso est confronté. Ces défis rendent d’ailleurs leur partenariat plus pertinent et nécessaire. Mais, « les ressources de la Banque mondiale, aussi importantes soient-elles, ne peuvent à elles seules répondre à l'ensemble des besoins », a-t-il souligné, saluant dans ce sens « les réformes audacieuses que le Burkina Faso est en train d’entreprendre pour accroître ses ressources domestiques à mobiliser et à allouer au financement de son propre développement ». Une vue des partenaires techniques et financiers « Je crois qu’aujourd’hui dans l’espace Union économique et monétaire ouest-africaine (Uémoa), le Burkina Faso est premier dans cet effort. Il est important de le relever et de le saluer et surtout d’encourager le Burkina Faso à rester dans cette voie et peut-être même à faire mieux pour inspirer les autres pays de la sous-région », a affirmé M. Diagana. Le Vice-Président de la Banque mondiale pour l'Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre s’est dit convaincu que « les financements extérieurs, qu’ils viennent des multilatéraux ou bilatéraux, quels que soient leurs volumes, leur signification, ils ne seraient jamais suffisants pour le financement total du développement. C’est l’effort national, les ressources nationales, les compétences nationales qui développent un pays ». La ministre Déléguée chargée du Budget, Fatoumata Bako/Traoré, ainsi que la dizaine d’autres membres du gouvernement qui ont pris la parole ont invité la Banque mondiale à plus de « flexibilité » et « d’adaptabilité » au regard des urgences auxquelles fait face le Burkina Faso. Ils ont à l’unanimité salué le sens d’écoute de l’équipe la Banque mondiale au Burkina Faso. « La relation entre le Burkina Faso et le Groupe de la Banque mondiale s'inscrit dans une histoire déjà riche. Elle a accompagné des transformations importantes de notre économie et de notre société, tout en s'adaptant aux défis auxquels notre pays est confronté », a laissé entendre Fatoumata Bako/Traoré, la représentante de Aboubakar Nacanabo, ministre burkinabè en charge de l'Economie et des Finance. La ministre Déléguée chargée du Budget, Fatoumata Bako-Traoré Elle a salué le fait que « le nouveau Cadre prévoit une flexibilité dans les localités d’intervention afin de tenir compte de l’évolution du contexte national et des besoins des populations. Cette capacité d’adaptation est importante pour assurer la pertinence et l’efficacité des interventions tout au long de la période couverte par le Cadre participatif ». Selon Fatoumata Bako/Traoré, les priorités retenues dans ce nouveau CPP 2026-2031 traduisent la volonté commune des deux parties de répondre à des besoins concrets tout en accompagnant les transformations que le Burkina Faso veut. Elle indiqué que trois domaines concentrent ainsi l'essentiel de cette ambition. « Le premier concerne la santé et l'éducation. Le deuxième porte sur l'accès à l'électricité et le troisième axe touche à la productivité agricole et à la sécurité alimentaire », a-t-elle déclaré. Une vue d'ensemble de la salle La Banque mondiale est convaincue que lorsque la vision est associée à la volonté politique du Gouvernement, à l'énergie et à la créativité des populations, les résultats seront au rendez-vous et une transformation profonde traduira cela en emplois. Le Groupe de la Banque mondiale a réitéré son engagement à être aux côtés et à répondre avec diligence et célérité aux besoins et aux priorités du pays. Par Bernard BOUGOUM L’article Développement: lancement du Cadre de Partenariat Pays 2026-2031 entre le Burkina Faso et la Banque mondiale est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.description: La sélection nationale marocaine des moins de 20 ans a décroché son billet pour la phase finale de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN U20), après sa victoire 2-0 face à l’Égypte, ce samedi, au stade de l’Autorité du canal de Suez, à Ismaïlia, dans le cadre de la quatrième journée du tournoi nord-africain qualificatif pour la compétition continentale. Les « Lionceaux de l’Atlas » ont ouvert le score à la 25e minute par l’intermédiaire d’Adam Baallal, avant que Sami Bouhoudane ne double la mise à la 33e minute. La sélection marocaine a ainsi regagné les vestiaires avec une avance de deux buts. En seconde période, les Égyptiens ont tenté de revenir au score et de réduire l’écart, mais la vigilance du gardien Belaârouch et de la défense marocaine les en a empêchés. De leur côté, les Marocains ont poursuivi leurs offensives à la recherche d’un troisième but. La sélection nationale a conservé son avantage et sa concentration jusqu’au coup de sifflet final, malgré les tentatives répétées de l’Égypte. Les « Lionceaux de l’Atlas » se sont finalement imposés 2-0, assurant ainsi leur qualification pour la phase finale de la CAN U20, avant de disputer leur dernier match face à la Libye. items.title: Don’t Write With AI , Say People Who Write With AI
items.description: The university where the term artificial intelligence was coined is ringing in the field’s 70th birthday in fitting fashion: with an academic-integrity scandal. Last month, Dartmouth College’s president, Sian Leah Beilock, published an essay in The Atlantic headlined: “Why I Want More AI at Dartmouth.” Now Beilock is launching a review of whether her top deputy used too much AI. On September 21, the student newspaper The Dartmouth reported that Provost Santiago Schnell appeared to have relied heavily on AI to write all nine of the articles he’s published this year—including a Washington Post op-ed about students outsourcing their writing to AI. Schnell’s response to the accusation didn’t help his cause. According to the student paper, he sent an email statement acknowledging that he uses AI chatbots as “assistive tools” in his writing but downplayed their role in his process. Even Schnell’s statement, the paper found, registered as “100% AI-written” on Pangram, an AI-detection service that is imperfect but boasts a very low error rate. A Dartmouth spokesperson told me that neither Beilock nor Schnell would comment for this story. [ Read: The pangram backlash unfolding on college campuses ] Schnell is the latest example of an ironic phenomenon: People whose job involves writing about the appropriate uses of AI—or even setting the rules on AI use for others—keep getting caught using AI to do it. There was the Australian university professor whose op-ed about the importance of students doing their own writing turned out to be at least partly AI-generated. There was the nonprofit executive whose book about the future of truth in the AI age turned out to include quotes fabricated by AI. There was the AI beat reporter who reportedly lost his job after he accidentally copied quotes invented by AI into one of his stories. And there was the Stanford misinformation expert who got upbraided by a judge when his declaration supporting an anti-AI-deepfake law turned out to contain ChatGPT-hallucinated citations. It’s one thing to embrace AI writing openly or shamelessly, like the billionaire financier who readily acknowledged the technology’s role in his Wall Street Journal op-ed (albeit only after it was discovered). It’s another to use AI to inveigh against improper uses of AI, and it raises an awkward question: Why do some of the people warning us most loudly about the technology’s pitfalls keep tumbling headfirst into them? I reached out to all five of the individuals listed above for an answer, but the only one who agreed to speak with me on the record was Steven Rosenbaum, the author of the book The Future of Truth: How AI Reshapes Reality and the executive director of the nonprofit Sustainable Media Center. Unlike some of the others, Rosenbaum disclosed his use of AI in the writing and editing process, and he has never tried to tell other people not to use it. But that didn’t save him from ignominy when The New York Times reported in May that the book was riddled with AI-generated misquotes. I spoke with him at the time, and he told me that he felt “betrayed” by ChatGPT. Five months on, Rosenbaum seems to have accepted a bit more responsibility for the mistakes. He told me that he is preparing to publish a revised version of his book with all of the errors corrected, an author’s note, and a new chapter on (what else?) AI hallucinations. He still believes that the fault lies more with the technology’s makers than its users, though. “As a technology, it is incredibly seductive,” he said. Rosenbaum said that he’d started out using AI to better understand the technology. He’d gradually come to rely on it as a writing partner that made the work both easier and less lonely. He described his experience of writing with AI as a messy process, one in which the work of the human and that of the machine get all tangled up. “The line between thinking and researching and reading and outlining and drafting and writing is really blurry,” he said. A simple solution, of course, would be not to use AI at all. Rosenbaum, however, has no interest in that. He said that he still plans to use chatbots as a writing companion—just “more carefully” now, double-checking all of their claims and citations before adopting them. He’s not alone in his unwillingness to abandon the tools that got him in trouble. Although each of the people caught using AI to warn about AI has commented publicly on the episode in some form, none responded by swearing off the technology. Rosenbaum, for his part, thinks we’re headed toward a world in which writing with AI is the norm and all that matters is the result. “I don’t think readers care how the sausage is made,” he said. “They care that it’s delicious.” I’m not so sure. I too have experimented with using AI as a research tool in my writing. But The Atlantic has a strict policy against the use of AI-generated prose, and so do I. I’ve found that having a personal red line is both useful and clarifying: I might ask a chatbot questions, get its feedback on a word choice or an explanation, or ask it to poke holes in my argument, but I will not ask it to write for me or use its writing in my own drafts. I think readers value knowing that every word they’re reading was chosen by the author and not an algorithm. That said, I can see how the distinction between using AI for research and writing could feel slippery to some. It’s conceivable, for instance, that a chatbot’s biases could be infiltrating my ideas, if not my precise words. (Then again, so could the biases of Google’s search-ranking engine or my social-media feeds.) I have another theory as to why people who caution others about AI seem to be using it themselves. In a scenario strikingly similar to the one at Dartmouth, the professor in charge of academic integrity at Western Sydney University wrote an op-ed in May on the importance of students not delegating their work to AI. “Don’t cut corners,” Cath Ellis, the university’s pro-vice-chancellor for quality and integrity, wrote in The Sydney Morning Herald . “Don’t outsource your thinking, however tempting that may be.” The op-ed, it soon became clear, had been generated at least partly by AI. In that case, a university spokesperson defended Ellis’s use of the technology as “sophisticated and appropriate,” because she had fed her own past work into the AI tool before asking it to help her draft the op-ed. Ellis told The Sydney Morning Herald that the op-ed hadn’t been written “by” AI: “It was written with AI, and there’s a really big difference there,” she said. Ellis’s excuse might ring hollow to the students she chastised, but it’s revealing to those of us trying to wrap our minds around the apparent hypocrisy . In her op-ed, Ellis implied that students who use AI to write are outsourcing their thinking. In defending her own AI use, she distinguished between the writing (which she outsourced) and the ideas (which she claimed were original). Likewise, Schnell fretted in his op-ed that “students can now produce proficient prose without performing much of the intellectual work the prose appears to represent.” Yet when confronted with his own AI use, he claimed authorship of the “ideas and arguments” even if bots did some of the writing. These guardians of academic integrity might be right that what they did is meaningfully different from a student simply feeding a professor’s assignment into a chatbot and handing in whatever it spits out. Of course, students can use AI in more nuanced ways too. No doubt plenty of students accused of AI cheating have mounted defenses that sounded a lot like Ellis’s and Schnell’s. Writing is thinking has become a common refrain among critics of those who use AI tools to do their writing. What we see again and again in defenses of AI writing is that the people using AI don’t seem to apply that maxim to themselves. And experts on the perils of AI fakery such as Rosenbaum and the Stanford misinformation expert, Jeff Hancock, appeared to have overestimated their own ability to steer clear of AI falsehoods. It’s reminiscent of what the sociologist W. Phillips Davison called the “third-person effect” in mass media: people’s tendency to believe that they’re immune to persuasive messaging even as they expect it to influence others. It is a form of hypocrisy, and it’s hard to feel much sympathy for thought leaders who get caught practicing what they preach against. But the fact that even professed AI experts blunder into overrelying on the technology suggests that Rosenbaum is onto something: Chatbots might come with fine-print disclaimers that they can make mistakes, but they bend over backwards in their interactions with users to come across as honest and trustworthy. It’s also true that society has yet to develop a vocabulary for all the ways of writing with AI that fall in between “AI-generated” and “entirely human-written.” Here’s where I acknowledge that even my own bright line on AI use might be fuzzier than I realize. In the process of writing this story, I described the thrust of my argument to Google and Claude and asked them for examples of AI-writing hypocrisy that I may have missed. Neither managed to surface any that I hadn’t previously been aware of. On a whim, I followed up with Claude by asking it to brainstorm some hypotheses as to why AI skeptics might fail to heed their own advice. I had my own ideas, and I had also solicited the thoughts of colleagues, but I wanted to see what the chatbot would come up with. One of its suggestions struck me as a sharper version of a thought I’d been struggling to formulate: “ Writing is thinking is a rule for other people,” it mused. I didn’t use Claude’s language, but the AI model had crisply summarized a notion I’d been thinking over. That formulation no doubt informed how I thought about this story’s framing. Am I an AI-writing hypocrite now too? I talked through some of this with a journalist who once got in trouble over a story that contained AI-generated errors. We corresponded on the condition of anonymity because they said that resurfacing the incident could damage their job prospects. This was the lesson they said they had learned: “AI is a power tool, and like any power tool it’s dangerous if you’re careless with it. You can be the guy who warned everyone that a table saw can cut your fingers off and still lose a finger one day, because that risk is built into the machine. It goes up the more you use it.” When you think about it that way, it makes sense that some of the people relying on AI would be the same ones sounding the alarm about its risks. They know its flaws, but they also know its power. And they just can’t bring themselves to give that up.

items.title: EOCO’s handling of arrests could cost NDC power – Kpebu
items.description: Private legal practitioner Martin Kpebu has warned that the conduct of the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) in handling arrest cases, including that of Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, could contribute to the National Democratic Congress (NDC) losing power within six years. His comments follow the continued detention of the MP after he voluntarily reported to EOCO on Thursday, October 1, following the issuance of a High Court warrant for his arrest. EOCO has said it is working with the Attorney-General’s Office to bring the MP before a weekend court. Speaking to the media on Saturday, October 3, Mr Kpebu commended Speaker of Parliament Alban Bagbin for insisting that the matter be handled in accordance with parliamentary procedures, despite his affiliation with the NDC. According to him, Parliament’s Standing Orders provide specific procedures for dealing with the arrest of a sitting MP, and he questioned why EOCO did not follow those processes. Mr Kpebu argued that the continued detention of the MP, coupled with what he described as errors in the handling of the case, could gradually erode public confidence in the government. He said although the NDC may retain power in the next election, dissatisfaction with the government’s conduct could build over time. “These things that they are doing, so you see how they start small, small. So by six years, then we get fed up with them,” he said. Mr Kpebu urged the government to learn from the experiences of previous administrations and avoid actions that could create public resentment. He also stressed the need for authorities to respect parliamentary procedures and ensure that investigations involving MPs are conducted within the law. His comments come amid concerns raised by Parliament over Mr Baffour Awuah’s continued detention, with the circumstances prompting questions about his rights, parliamentary privileges and the independence of Parliament.

items.title: Fury to invite Trump to lead ring walk before Joshua showdown
items.description: Former heavyweight champion Tyson Fury will invite US President Donald Trump to lead his ring walk before his clash with British rival Anthony Joshua. Fury and Joshua are set to fight in Cardiff on December 11 and the self-styled ‘Gypsy King’ is keen for Trump to join the procession to the ring at the 80,000-capacity Principality Stadium. Fury met Trump at the UFC Freedom 250 at the White House in June and wore a cap emblazoned with the words “Donald Trump for Prime Minister” after having his United States travel ban lifted by the 80-year-old. “I’ll definitely make that offer to my old buddy, old pal, and we’ll see if he’s available,” Fury said. “Probably unlikely because of the situation he’s in at the moment, being the President of the United States.” Meanwhile, Fury insists his clash with Joshua is merely preparation for his true priority — a trilogy fight against Oleksandr Usyk, to whom he has lost twice already. “I don’t have any intention of retiring after Joshua. I’m using this bum as a warm-up for Usyk,” he said. “This is a bum to me and I can guarantee that on the night when I knock him spark out he won’t know what time it is. And then I want the rabbit (Usyk) in New York City. “This year will be the most active year for me since 2018. I’ve done 12 rounds with a 6ft 8in Arslanbek Makhmudov and I’ve done seven rounds with another 6ft 7in behemoth in Mariusz Wach. “Let’s not pull any punches here. I’m firing on all cylinders at the moment. I feel fantastic. I’m 38 years young.” The post Fury to invite Trump to lead ring walk before Joshua showdown appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pape Gueye : « C’est une position que j’ai prise et que j’allais assumer »
items.description: Ce dimanche 4 octobre 2026, le Sénégal affronte les Comores en match amical au stade Vélodrome de Marseille. Présent en conférence de presse d’avant-match, Pape Gueye est revenu sur sa décision d’arrêter en équipe nationale après la Coupe du monde 2026. Après l’élimination du Sénégal au Mondial 2026, Pape Gueye avait fait une annonce choc : prendre une pause avec les Lions, si des choses ne changeaient pas autour de la Tanière. Néanmoins, le milieu de terrain est revenu après le départ du staff précédent et l’arrivée de Patrick Vieira. Le joueur de Vieira est revenu sur cet épisode, ce samedi 3 octobre 2026. Interrogé sur les raisons de cette annonce, le gaucher s’est expliqué. « La réponse se trouve dans votre question. Aujourd’hui, si je suis là, c’est une position que j’ai prise et que j’allais assumer. Aujourd’hui, je suis très content d’être ici et je vais faire de mon mieux pour aider cette équipe. Je pense que c’est le plus important. Peut-être que si je le souhaite, il y aura l’occasion d’en parler, mais ce n’est pas le plus important aujourd’hui. Comme l’a dit le coach, il y a un nouveau staff qui est là. On travaille bien, tout le monde est à l’écoute à l’entraînement. On essaye de tout mettre en place pour respecter ce que le coach demande. Comme il l’a dit, ça demande du temps. C’est vrai qu’on est habitués, nous les Sénégalais, à gagner sur les dernières années. C’est quelque chose de bien, mais il faut du temps pour qu’on redevienne, entre guillemets, cette équipe… » Pape Gueye a par ailleurs évoqué ce match contre les Comores au Vélodrome, dans un stade qu’il connaît parfaitement. « J’ai fait quatre ans dans ce club, j’ai pas mal de souvenirs qui reviennent. Je pense que ça va être quelque chose de bien pour nous, notamment aussi pour les Comoriens, de jouer dans ce magnifique stade. L’Olympique de Marseille, c’est un club qui m’a fait grandir en tant que footballeur, mais en tant que personne aussi. On sait que quand on joue à Marseille, ce n’est pas très simple, mais ça m’a permis aujourd’hui d’être le joueur que je suis. Donc c’est que du bonheur. Il y aura ma famille, mes amis. Après, ce qui a pu se passer à Marseille, c’est le football. » O.B.N

items.title: Tunisie-Canada | Vers un partenariat renforcé dans le domaine de la formation médicale
items.description: Dans le cadre du renforcement des liens académiques et scientifiques entre la Tunisie et le Canada, Lassaad Boutara, ambassadeur de Tunisie au Canada, a présidé une réunion virtuelle stratégique. Réunissant l’équipe diplomatique de l'ambassade ainsi que les Doyens des Facultés de médecine de Tunis, Sousse, Monastir et Sfax, cette rencontre organisée, mercredi 30 septembre 2026, visait à structurer une feuille de route commune pour la coopération médicale institutionnelle. Les échanges ont principalement porté sur l'identification des priorités et le développement d'opportunités de partenariat avec le Collège Royal des Médecins et Chirurgiens du Canada. Plusieurs axes de collaboration clés ont été établis, précise l'ambassade tunisienne, en citant : Le dveloppement de la formation médicale postgraduée, formation continue des formateurs, innovation pédagogique et renforcement de l’apprentissage de la médecine en langue anglaise. La dynamisation de la mobilité des enseignants, des chercheurs et des médecins résidents, à travers des programmes d'échanges académiques et des stages de courte durée. L'élaboration de programmes de recherche conjoints et intégration de l’intelligence artificielle appliquée aux technologies médicales. La coopération en matière d’assurance qualité, de certification et d’accréditation des cursus de santé. Cette initiative marque une étape importante dans la modernisation de l'enseignement médical tunisien et l'ouverture de nouvelles perspectives internationales pour les praticiens et universitaires des deux pays, a commenté l'ambassade. Y. N. L’article Tunisie-Canada | Vers un partenariat renforcé dans le domaine de la formation médicale est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Why Tinubu may win 2027 election – The Economist; ‘Forecast isn’t verdict,’ ADC reacts
items.description: The Economist has predicted that despite the economic woes besetting Nigeria and the people’s discontent, President Bola Tinubu may still win the forthcoming 2027 election. Read Also: NIGERIA @ 66: Judiciary – Last or lost hope of common man? However, reacting, the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council rejected The Economist’s report, noting that “A forecast is not a verdict.” Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, made the party’s stand known in an article titled “No forecast can overrule the people: Nigerians will vote out Tinubu and elect Atiku”. He said: “These factors matter. But they are not the same as public consent, and none can tell us how Nigerians will vote in January. A forecast is not a verdict. “Nigerians measure the economy by what their income can buy, what they must go without and whether they can provide a decent life for their families.” On the prediction that low voters’ turnout could favour Tinubu, Shaibu noted that the low participation recorded in the 2023 presidential election could be due to apathy, insecurity, distrust, logistical barriers or the belief that votes would not count. Therefore, he said, it should not be interpreted as evidence that most Nigerians support an incumbent. “Tinubu won the election; he did not receive the votes of most registered voters,” he added. The Economist’s forecast In its October 1 report, The Economist posited that worsening security crisis, the effects of economic reforms, and political challengers should work against the president’s re-election bid. However, it noted that “On the face of it, Mr Tinubu’s cool is surprising. “Incumbents, with access to the ruling-party machinery and plentiful cash to dole out goodies, have tended to have an advantage in recent Nigerian elections.” Another factor that The Economist said could work for President Tinubu is religion. Running on a Muslim-Muslim ticket could give him large votes in the North, it said. Furthermore, the report added: “As long as the security crisis remains unresolved and economic growth, which is expected to hit 4.1% this year, does not translate into concrete improvements in Nigerians’ daily lives, many voters will remain disappointed. Yet few will use the ballot box to express their disappointment.” Another factor is that although many in the South-West are disappointed with the Tinubu administration, the fact that he is their son would count in the President’s favour. items.title: Health sovereignty a priority for 1.4b Africans – President Mahama declares
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has urged African leaders to make health sovereignty a priority for their country as part of a broader strategy for the continent to achieve health sovereignty. He said it was about time that Africa stopped treating health as a charitable cost and positioned it as an investable, high-growth economic sector. Speaking at the Alamein Africa Forum on Saturday in El Alamein, Egypt today (Saturday, October 3, 2026), President Mahama added that Africa’s goal must be the health sovereignty and economic and fiscal security of its 1.4 billion people. “Our goal is health sovereignty, and economic and fiscal security of 1.4 billion African people. For decades, African finance ministers and global investors have made a fundamental error. They have treated health as a line-item cost and a social expenditure in their budgets to be funded only when there is money left over. “Today, at the Alamein Africa Forum, we are moving beyond that outdated perspective. Health is not a charitable cost. It is an investable, high-growth economic sector,” he said. Health investment President Mahama underscored the need to invest in health, stating that it drives human capital, manufacturing, job creation and macroeconomic stability while citing global evidence. “The arithmetic is indisputable. The Copenhagen Consensus showed that a targeted package of basic emergency maternal and newborn care can yield $87 in economic and social returns for every single dollar that is invested. The Lancet Commission established that falling mortality rates accounted for nearly a quarter of total income growth in developing economies in the early 2000s,” he said. He pointed to Africa’s dangerous dependency, stating that the continent imports over 70 per cent of its pharmaceuticals and nearly 99 per cent of its vaccines, with tens of billions of dollars leaving African economies annually to purchase medicines abroad. President Mahama indicated that traditional donor assistance is declining, with OECD projections indicating health aid will decrease by 29 to 46 per cent compared to 2024 levels. He, however, indicated that governments cannot fund the transition alone and called for private capital, industrial developers, commercial banks and sovereign funds to participate, through initiatives like Business United for Mothers, Babies, and Youth, championed by President Samia Suluhu Hassan of Tanzania. He urged African leaders and stakeholders to stop treating health as an expense item in their budgets, and build the factories, integrate supply chains, fund innovators, and secure the future of their citizens. AfCFTA The President affirmed that the argument for the development of a vibrant local pharmaceutical manufacturing sector rested on four pillars, including a captive market set to grow to 2.5 billion people by 2050, saving foreign exchange through import substitution, and the single continental market offered by the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). “The African Continental Free Trade Area and African manufacturing plants do not serve a single country of 10 or 30 million. It serves a single unified market of 1.4 billion consumers,” he said. President Mahama cited the Africa CDC’s first pooled tender for maternal and child health products, which, by aggregating demand, achieved price reductions of more than 30 per cent while ensuring African manufacturers won 50 percent of product lines. He said health sovereignty means health security for citizens, high-value jobs and affordability, noting Africa’s structural paradox where nearly one million trained healthcare professionals and science graduates remain unemployed despite a shortage of 6 million health workers, according to the WHO. Continental initiatives President Mahama pointed to Egypt’s elimination of hepatitis C, which dropped prevalence from 10 percent to under 0.5 per cent by negotiating technology transfer and building domestic production through champions like Eva Pharma, and treating 4 million citizens locally, making Egypt the first country recognized by WHO on the path to eliminating hepatitis C. He also cited Nigeria’s African Medical Centre of Excellence in Abuja, pioneered by Afreximbank and King’s College Hospital, tackling the $6 billion annual loss to outbound medical tourism. On Ghana, he said the government is implementing the Accra Reset by expanding the National Health Insurance Scheme, introducing the free primary health care programme, establishing the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (MahamaCares), and empowering the Food and Drugs Authority and the National Vaccine Institute to transition Ghana from a consumer to a producer of health products. To scale up such successes, he announced a new continental enabler. “Today, we present the Health Investment and National Gateway, acronym HINGE, Enabler. Developed with the African Medicines Agency, Institute Pasteur, and Afrochampions, HINGE will become a digital platform that streamlines regulations, clinical validation, and commercialisation into a unified process for innovators and investors,” he said. He added that through the Accra Reset Presidential Council, dedicated task forces and reformed inter-ministerial observatories will track capital flows, enforce policy commitments and dismantle non-tariff barriers across regional value chains.

items.title: Any man who says he won’t die for his woman is a fool — Odumodublvck
items.description: Nigerian rapper Tochukwu Ojogwu, popularly known as Odumodublvck, has said any man who claims he would not die for his woman is a “fool.” The rapper made the statement during an episode of the In Motion Podcast on YouTube, shared on Friday, while discussing his views on relationships and his controversial feud with fellow rapper Blaqbonez. “Any man wey talk say he no fit die for him woman na fool!” Odumodublvck said. Explaining his position from a Christian perspective, he said men were expected to love their wives sacrificially, just as Christ loved the church. “Because me now, I’m a Christian. See, this is my power. And Jesus said, Christ said we should love our wife like Christ loved the church. And what did Christ do for the church? He died for the church,” he said. The rapper also said he expected to die before his wife because she is younger than him. “I’m probably going to die before my wife, in Jesus’ name. Amen… Why should my wife die before me? When she’s younger than me? Doesn’t make any sense. I should die before my wife,” he said. According to him, his wife would take care of their children and continue whatever he had started after his death. “And when I die, it’s my wife that will now take everything and distribute to my children so there will not be wahala. So it’s my wife that will continue whatever it is that I started,” he said. Odumodublvck also attributed his attitude towards women and money to his upbringing, saying his mother’s generosity had influenced him. “Like me now, my mom is a cheerful giver. If you give me one million Naira now, before you know it, I’ve sent it to ten people. I don’t know how to hold money. So my girlfriend will be holding my money for me,” he said. He compared the importance of women in relationships to the queen in chess, describing the queen as the strongest piece on the board. “So if you don’t understand the concept of loving a woman and putting a woman where a woman is meant to be. Like if you look at chess, the strongest piece on the board is the queen,” he said. “If the queen goes, just forget that game. Forget the game. The king is exposed,” he added. The rapper also addressed the perception that he is a misogynist, describing the label as unfair. “They think I’m a misogynist,” he said. Asked whether the perception bothered him, Odumodublvck replied, “It bothers me a lot. A whole lot. Because it’s such an unfair thing to say.” He then questioned whether someone willing to die for his partner could be described as a misogynist. “Okay, now I want to die for my girlfriend. Will a misogynist die for his woman?” he asked. The post Any man who says he won’t die for his woman is a fool — Odumodublvck appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NACOC begins pre-screening checks at Accra International Airport
items.description: Ghana Airports Company Limited has announced that pre-screening checks by the Narcotics Control Commission are now being conducted at the entrance to the Departure Hall at Accra International Airport before passengers proceed to check-in. In a public notice issued on October 2, the GACL said all passengers travelling through the airport will be required to undergo luggage screening at the entrance to departures before entering the departure hall. Screening is conducted using scanning machines and sniffer dogs as part of enhanced security measures. The GACL noted that pre-screening checks are conducted at several international airports worldwide. To ensure that these additional security procedures are completed without unnecessary pressure on passengers ahead of their flights, all departing passengers are advised to arrive at the airport at least three hours before their scheduled departure time. This will allow adequate time for security screening, check-in, and other boarding formalities. The GACL further stated that access to the Departure Hall is restricted to travelling passengers only, and non-travelling persons will not be permitted entry. The company expressed appreciation for the cooperation and understanding of all passengers and airport users as it continues to work with security agencies to strengthen security and ensure safe, secure, and efficient airport operations.

items.title: Tennessee prison chief who oversaw botched execution resigns: governor
items.description: The prison commissioner in the southern US state of Tennessee has resigned over the botched execution of convicted murderer Christa Pike, Governor Bill Lee said on Saturday. Lee said in a statement that commissioner Frank Strada would leave his post this month. Pike’s lawyers say she is in critical condition, unconscious and on a ventilator in a hospital, after her execution by lethal injection went wrong on Wednesday. Pike, 50, survived two injections of the normally lethal substance pentobarbital as punishment for the murder of Colleen Slemmer in 1995. It was the second failed execution in Tennessee this year. The state halted an execution in May after medical staff failed to tap a vein in the prisoner’s arm. Lee said he thanked Strada for “his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment”. In the same statement, Strada said, “I continue to believe the Department (of Correction) carried out its responsibilities in accordance with the established protocol.” Lee, who previously denied Pike clemency, has halted further executions through the rest of the year while a review is conducted. Had the drugs killed Pike, she would have been the first woman executed by the state in more than two centuries. In the United States, only 18 women have been executed since 1976, according to the Death Penalty Information Centre.

items.title: ‘I was stepping up into an alliance’ – Sammy Crabbe clarifies John Boadu backing
items.description: Chairmanship aspirant of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Sammy Crabbe, has clarified that his decision to align with fellow aspirant John Boadu ahead of the party’s national executive elections was not a withdrawal from the race. Speaking to JoyNews at the party’s National Delegates Conference in Kumasi, Mr Crabbe said the arrangement was the result of discussions with Mr Boadu as well as consultations with his team and supporters. He said the decision was taken after considering how their respective programmes and experience in party management could be brought together. “That’s all it is. Yeah, exactly that. Nothing more,” he said when asked whether there were external considerations or influences behind the alliance. Mr Crabbe explained that although the decision was reached on the morning of the congress, discussions had started earlier and he had to consult his supporters before formalising the arrangement. Read also: Sammy Crabbe steps down from NPP Chairmanship race, backs John Boadu “It happened this morning, but it didn’t start this morning. I had to also sit down with my team and supporters because you want to bring people along. It’s important that you explain to them what you are thinking, what is happening,” he said. He said the consultations were followed by discussions on how to properly communicate the arrangement after an earlier impression emerged that he had simply withdrawn from the chairmanship contest. Mr Crabbe said that was not the case, stressing that he was “stepping up into an alliance.” “We also sat down and come up, design a joint statement that actually corrected an earlier impression that I had just stepped down or whatever. No. I was stepping up into an alliance,” he said. The clarification follows a post by Mr Boadu on X, formerly Twitter, which indicated that Mr Crabbe had stepped down from the race and endorsed him. Mr Crabbe’s subsequent signed statement described the arrangement as an alliance aimed at promoting unity of purpose within the NPP. Under the arrangement, he urged his supporters to vote for Mr Boadu, while pledging to work alongside him to implement their programmes. The NPP is holding its National Delegates Conference at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi, where delegates are voting to elect nine national executive officers. A total of 7,163 delegates are expected to participate in the elections across 31 polling stations.

items.title: Fernandes hails Portugal’s ‘greatest symbol’ Ronaldo, calls for unity
items.description: Portugal playmaker Bruno Fernandes said Cristiano Ronaldo remains the country’s greatest footballing icon despite walking out on the squad this week after finding out he would not start a match. The 41-year-old superstar said Wednesday he had left the team after coach Jorge Jesus said Ronaldo would not start against Denmark in the Nations League, a match Portugal won 4-2 without him. Former Real Madrid and Manchester United attacker Ronaldo’s future with the national team, for whom he is the leading goalscorer and most capped player, is in doubt after his walk out. “Regarding Cristiano, I had a conversation with him, and what I told him, and what I repeat here, is this — the most important thing is that, regardless of what happens, Cristiano Ronaldo will never cease to be the greatest symbol of our national team, of our football, and of the country, for what he has done not only in Portugal but throughout the world,” Fernandes told reporters Saturday. Manchester United midfielder Fernandes called for unity after a tumultuous few days in which Portugal fans’ opinions have been split over Ronaldo’s decision. “He has a reserved place not only among the best of all time, but also in the hearts of all Portuguese people, and the most important thing is that we stop dividing things,” said Fernandes. “There are no divisions in the national team, it is one and will remain so, despite any noise that may come from outside… “We are outside of this controversy, but what I ask is that the country does not divide itself, does not make choices, that it respects all sides, but, at the same time, Cris is and will be the biggest icon of our national team, he deserves everyone’s respect, regardless of who likes him more or (who likes him) less.” Portugal beat Norway and Denmark away from home without Ronaldo starting and face Norway again on Sunday. Coach Jesus said Ronaldo was a “symbol of Portugal” and said there would be time to speak about him after Sunday’s game in Porto. “I’m going to focus on the team, on the opponent which is Norway, one of the five best teams in Europe. That’s the problem right now,” said the 72-year-old coach. The post Fernandes hails Portugal’s ‘greatest symbol’ Ronaldo, calls for unity appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Par ici la porte, CR7 ? (Le billet de Omar DIOUF)
items.description: Savoir écouter son corps, écrivions-nous lors du dernier Mondial en Amérique. Au coup de sifflet final du match Portugal-Rdc, en juin dernier, des amateurs de foot avaient moqué les maigres statistiques de la star Cristiano Ronaldo : aucun dribble ni tir cadré vers le but, juste 25 ballons touchés durant toute la rencontre. Un air de déclin pour CR7 qui, disions-nous, à 41 ans, participait à sa 6e Coupe du monde. C’était le moment idéal pour fermer la porte et dire adieu à la sélection portugaise. Mais non, le dandy du ballon rond a encore traîné ses savates dans le vestiaire et affiché son éternel coup de blues sur le banc, en faisant la moue même après les victoires de ses coéquipiers après deux matchs de Ligue des Nations Uefa. Son coach, Jorge Jesus, lui a alors presque ouvert la porte et montré la sortie. En football, rappelions-nous, il revient aux coaches de dire merci aux « vieux » joueurs pour services rendus à la nation, en les mettant sur la touche ou en les renvoyant à la maison, pour faire la place aux plus jeunes sur la pelouse. Alors, « adeus » la légende CR7 ? omar.diouf@lesoleil.sn

items.title: American High School Students Are Selling Guns Bound for Cartels
Turn CSIR research into commercially viable products for national dev’t – Dr Agyeman-Rawlings
items.description: The Minister of Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation, Dr Zaneto Agyeman-Rawlings, has called for stronger collaboration between the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), the Government and the private sector to translate research into commercially viable products for national development. There was the need to bridge the gap between scientific research and the public to enable Ghanaians and the private sector to understand, access and benefit from innovations developed by Ghanaian scientists and researchers, she said. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings made the call during a working visit to the CSIR in Accra as part of her familiarisation tour of agencies and institutions under the Ministry. The tour, she said, was to enable her to better understand the environment, people and work of the agencies through direct and interactive engagements. The Minister said the CSIR had immense potential to contribute to Ghana’s development, noting that it already had expertise and research covering a wide range of sectors. “There’s a disconnect between research and academia and the public. Because of that disconnect, sometimes it is difficult for us to help the private sector tap into what you’re doing,” she said. She, therefore, urged the CSIR to work closely with the Ministry’s Public Relations Directorate to showcase its research, innovations and products at the Ministry and through its communication platforms. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings said the Ministry intended to display samples of products developed by CSIR institutes, including agricultural products, cereals and other innovations, at its reception to enable visitors to see and appreciate its work. “We want people to know who you are. We want people to know what you do. We want us to celebrate your scientists, your researchers,” she said. She said the Ministry would also use its social media platforms, screens, display panels and website to showcase the work of scientists and researchers. The Minister said the initiative would make science more relatable, particularly to young people, and encourage them to consider science as a broad career field with practical applications. She said the Ministry was also working to make its website more engaging, including featuring scientists of the month, quarter or year and their research. The Minister expressed concern that Ghana sometimes sought technologies from outside the country when similar solutions already existed within CSIR. She said the country needed to identify and support existing local technologies and create opportunities for the private sector to invest in and commercialise them. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings also called for increased attention to research and development, saying Ghana needed to work towards the African Union’s target of spending one per cent of Gross Domestic Product on research and development. She said although funding constraints remained a challenge, scientists and researchers also needed to make a stronger case for investment by demonstrating the practical and economic value of their work. The Minister said she was particularly interested in research and pilot projects that could support the remediation of degraded lands, purification of polluted water bodies, and protection of the environment. She encouraged the various CSIR institutes to review their research archives and identify innovations that could be showcased and developed into scalable and economically viable projects to safeguard the environment for future generations. She also acknowledged concerns raised about retaining scientists and researchers, saying conditions of service were important but would have to be considered within the broader context of the institution’s financial sustainability. “If you can commercialise what you do and we can make a case for you retaining more of what you get, you can decide on how to improve your conditions. So it is a collaborative effort,” she said. She urged CSIR staff to communicate their challenges openly to the Ministry but, where possible, accompany those challenges with proposed solutions. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings, said she looked forward to visiting all 13 CSIR institutes across the country to understand their research, challenges and potential contributions to national development. Professor Paul P. Bosu, Director-General of CSIR, said the Minister’s visit was particularly significant at a time when Ghana was looking with renewed urgency to science, technology and innovation as instruments for addressing national challenges and accelerating socio-economic development. He said CSIR had built a rich reservoir of scientific expertise over seven decades in agriculture, natural resources, environment, industry, energy, food and nutrition, biotechnology and other areas critical to national development. Prof. Bosu said climate change, new technologies, artificial intelligence, biotechnology and advanced materials were transforming economies and creating new opportunities. “Ghana cannot afford to be merely a consumer of knowledge and technology. We must increasingly become a producer, an innovator and a problem solver,” he said. He pledged CSIR’s readiness to become an even stronger partner to government by providing scientific evidence for policymaking, developing technologies to address national needs, supporting industry and entrepreneurship, and promoting commercialisation. Prof. Bosu said the 13 specialised institutes under the Council were located in Accra, Kumasi, Bunsu, Kade, and Nyankpala, among other areas, supported by about 60 field stations. He invited the Minister to visit the institutes to gain first-hand knowledge of the breadth of CSIR’s work. Mr Mark Taylor, Chairman of the CSIR Governing Council, said the institution remained committed to turning research into practical solutions for Ghana’s development. He said CSIR faced challenges including the retention of scientific talent, inadequate research logistics and infrastructure, environmental degradation, and the need to move research outputs into commercial ventures. He said CSIR was ready to provide technical support for efforts to restore forests and polluted water bodies and to develop alternative livelihood strategies.

items.title: Baffour Awuah thanks Bawumia, NPP supporters after GH¢10m bail
items.description: Manhyia South Member of Parliament Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah has thanked Ghanaians, the leadership of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), his parliamentary colleagues, family and supporters for the solidarity shown to him following his detention by the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO). In a Facebook post on Saturday, October 3, Nana Baffour Awuah said he was “deeply grateful for the overwhelming support, prayers and solidarity” shown to him. He also expressed appreciation to Ghanaians who, he said, had “seen through the Government’s propaganda and stood firmly with me.” The MP specifically thanked NPP flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, his fellow Members of Parliament, the party’s leadership and entire membership, as well as his family, friends and sympathisers. His message follows his appearance before court in connection with the ongoing EOCO investigation. Nana Baffour Awuah has been granted GH¢10 million bail with two sureties after pleading not guilty to three charges brought against him by EOCO. The sureties are the Member of Parliament for Bosome Freho and the Member of Parliament for Effia. He denied charges of conspiracy to commit a crime and dissipation of public funds, intentionally causing financial loss to the state and money laundering, including an allegation that he facilitated the transfer of GH¢1 million to the then Managing Director of SIC Life in 2024.

items.title: Le parti Kiiraay affiche ses ambitions et reitére le patriotisme républicain au cœur de sa ligne
items.description: La première Université d’hivernage du parti Kiiraay, organisée sous le format « Think Tank » a permis, ce 3 octobre, aux responsables de préciser leur ligne politique. Ils ont par ailleurs défendu les réformes engagées par leur leader, le Président Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Un cap a été enfin fixé, en vue des prochaines échéances électorales. Superviseur général du Kiiraay, Aminata Touré a donné le ton en réaffirmant l’attachement du parti au respect de la Constitution. « L’Assemblée nationale ne peut pas voter de lois anticonstitutionnelles », a-t-elle déclaré, assurant que Kiiraay veillera « au strict respect de la Constitution, ainsi qu’à la préservation et à la défense de la République ». Elle a également dénoncé le recours à l’immunité parlementaire pour attaquer les institutions. Aminata Toure annonce un objectif électoral assumé qui consiste à « gagner 80 % des communes en 2027 ». Elle a par ailleurs indiqué que plus de 500 partis et organisations ont fusionné au sein de Kiiraay. Dans le prolongement des échanges, Alain Diouf, ministre auprès du Président de la République chargé du Suivi et de l’Évaluation de l’Agenda national de transformation Sénégal 2050, a mis en avant l’agenda réformateur du chef de l’État, Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Il a cité plusieurs chantiers engagés « en un temps record », notamment la réforme du Code des impôts, du Code de l’investissement, de la loi sur le patrimoine, de l’accès à l’information et du Code du travail. Sur le plan social, il a indiqué que 500 000 ménages vulnérables bénéficient actuellement d’un soutien de plus de 100 000 FCFA par trimestre, avec un objectif d’extension à un million de ménages, soit un impact annoncé sur environ 8 millions de personnes. La dimension doctrinale du parti a ensuite été réitérée par Alioune Dione, membre fondateur de Kiiraay, pour qui le « patriotisme républicain » ne saurait être « une attitude sectaire ou partisane », mais doit s’inscrire dans « le commun vouloir-vivre ensemble ». L’intérêt national prime sur les intérêts partisans Me Abdoulaye Tine, coordonnateur des cadres, a prolongé cette définition en plaçant l’intérêt national au-dessus des intérêts partisans. Il a défendu une conception du cadre politique fondée sur le respect de la loi, y compris dans le rapport à l’adversaire. « Le pouvoir n’est pas une propriété » et l’action politique ne doit reposer ni sur les « coups bas », ni sur l’insulte ou la fabrication de faits, a-t-il indiqué. La structuration territoriale constitue également un axe majeur. Mamadou Thiaw, superviseur général adjoint chargé des élus, a insisté sur la place centrale des maires dans l’organisation de Kiiraay. Il a appelé à une implication accrue des élus afin que « la voix des territoires soit pleinement entendue », allant jusqu’à annoncer la disponibilité des élus locaux du mouvement à contribuer à l’obtention d’une majorité parlementaire pour le président de la République. Moussa Bala Fofana, membre fondateur de Kiraay, a appelé les cadres à investir davantage les instances territoriales et les conseils des pôles, afin de participer à la mise en place de la gouvernance portée par le mouvement. À travers cette première Université d’hivernage, les débats sont globalement articulés autour de trois axes. Il s’agit de la défense de la République et de la Constitution, accompagnement des réformes de l’État et implantation territoriale, avec en ligne de mire les échéances électorales de 2027. O.BA
