items.title: Abducted NYSC Members: Parents accuse transport firm of withholding passengers’ next-of-kin details
items.description: By Adeola Badru Parents of prospective National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, members abducted by gunmen in Imo State have accused the transport company that conveyed their children from Ibadan of allegedly withholding vital passenger information when they approached its office for assistance, raising fresh questions about the firm’s handling of the incident. Read Also: NYSC members’ abduction: Tinubu’s alleged laxity emboldening terrorists — Makinde campaign The parents said they visited Eduak King Transport Company at Samonda, Ibadan, in a desperate search for information that could help them contact other affected families. However, the company refused to provide the next-of-kin list of passengers aboard the ill-fated vehicle, despite the emergency created by the abduction. One of the affected mothers, Mrs Iyabo Akande, whose daughter, Kehinde Marufat Akande, was among the abducted graduates, called on the Inspector-General of Police and the government to investigate the transport operator and ensure that those found culpable were held accountable. She said: “Please, our government, please, the Inspector General of Police, the transport company Eduak King located at Samonda, please help us investigate them and put fear into them. Call them to account. “Yesterday morning at their office, we were asking for the next of kin list so we could contact other parents, but they refused to present it or assist us. The company’s driver, Jeremiah, took our children. They must be held accountable.” Another parent, Engr. Olawale Olaleye, whose daughter was also among the victims, expressed concern over what he described as the company’s continued transport operations despite the abduction and the distress of the affected families. He said the parents were surprised to find the company loading another vehicle when they visited its premises to seek information and assistance. “We went to Samonda, to Eduak King. Surprisingly, they were already loading another vehicle. People are complaining, the company should be held liable.” When the transport company’s premises were visited, other transport operators were seen conducting their normal activities, while the premises of the affected company were locked and no official was available to respond to the allegations. The allegations came amid growing anxiety among families following the reported abduction of 19 prospective corps members who were travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to the NYSC permanent orientation camp in Abia State. The young graduates had boarded a bus operated by Eduak King Transport Company at its Samonda park on their way to begin the mandatory one-year national service after completing their university education. According to accounts provided by the affected families, the journey included an overnight stop around Onitsha, Anambra State, before the vehicle reportedly resumed its journey at about 4:00 am. The bus was allegedly attacked around the Owerri axis of Imo State at about 7:00 am, with 19 prospective corps members reportedly taken into the bush, while some other passengers escaped or were rescued. Among those abducted were graduates of Ladoke Akintola University of Technology (LAUTECH), Ogbomoso, including a set of twins. One of the parents, Engr. Olawale Olaleye, whose daughter was among those abducted, appealed to President Bola Tinubu and Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde to intervene urgently, lamenting that the reported ransom demand had left the families helpless. “The vehicle took off on Friday. They slept over around Onitsha. After taking off again around 4:00 am, after reaching Owerri in Imo State, they were kidnapped. That was where we heard information about her last.” Expressing frustration over the reported ransom demand, Olaleye said, “This morning, they are already demanding N50 million! N50 million for just one head! We don’t have mouth to talk too much, but please come to our rescue. Governor Seyi Makinde, President Tinubu, please come to our rescue. Since Thursday, I have not eaten, I can’t even sleep.” Another affected mother, Mrs Rebecca Adewale, whose 26-year-old son, Paul Iyanuoluwa Adewale, was among the abducted graduates, said the incident had thrown her family into deep anguish. She said the family had made enormous sacrifices to educate their son and expressed concern about the reported ransom demand, appealing to the authorities to intensify efforts to secure his release. Adewale also questioned the practice of deploying young graduates to distant locations for the compulsory national service, particularly in view of the security challenges associated with interstate journeys. Her husband, Omotosho Emmanuel Adewale, recounted how the family discovered their son’s abduction after several unanswered telephone calls. According to him, the family eventually received a brief call from Paul, who appeared to be communicating under the control of his captors and disclosed the ransom demand before the call ended. He appealed to the government to intervene urgently and ensure the safe return of their son and the other abducted graduates. Similarly, another parent, Mrs Iyabo Akande, said her daughter, Kehinde Marufat Akande, was travelling with her twin sister when the bus was attacked. She explained that the family had spoken with her daughter late at night during the overnight stop before receiving the distressing information the following morning. Akande said, “My name is Mrs Iyabo Akande, I am a trader. One of my twins, Kehinde Marufat Akande, was in that Abia-bound bus that was attacked in Imo State. We spoke around 11:00 pm when she sent a video of where they were sleeping overnight.“ “By morning around 5:00 am, they moved. The next thing we saw on our WhatsApp group at 6:17 am was a flashing alert/message from the kidnappers.” She disclosed that the abductors subsequently contacted her and demanded N50 million for her daughter’s release, followed by other financial demands. According to her, the family eventually transferred N100,000 after the abductors demanded money, hoping that the payment would prevent the captives from being harmed. She added that the kidnappers later requested money to provide food for the hostages, prompting some of the affected families to contribute funds in the hope of ensuring better treatment for their children in captivity. Akande lamented that the families lacked the financial capacity to meet the reported N50 million ransom demand and appealed to the government to intervene. Another parent, Deaconess Kemi Makinde, a trader, recalled taking her child to the Samonda motor park early in the morning to board the bus heading for the NYSC orientation camp. “My name is Deaconess Makinde, I am a trader. I took my child to the car park at Samonda on Tuesday morning around 5:00 am to 9:00 am to board the bus heading for the NYSC orientation camp. We are in complete agony, praying for their safe return.” Also speaking, Mr Bafunsho Olayiwola, a psychiatric healthcare personnel at the State Hospital, Ring Road, Ibadan, appealed to Nigerians and the authorities to intervene urgently to secure the release of the abducted graduates. He said, “Bandits came out to kidnap them. Ten were rescued on the spot, the remaining 19 were taken inside the bush. This morning, they asked him to bring N50 million. How will I get N50 million as per the kind of job I am doing for now? “We are imploring everybody, all well-meaning Nigerians, Governor Seyi Makinde, President Tinubu, help us rescue our children!” Meanwhile, the Executive Assistant to Governor Seyi Makinde on Security, CP Sunday Odukoya (retd.), has assured the affected families that the Oyo State Government is working with relevant security agencies to secure the release of the abducted prospective corps members. Odukoya, who addressed the parents at the state secretariat, said the government was monitoring the situation and had established security contacts with relevant authorities in Imo and Abia states, as well as military and federal intelligence agencies. He assured the parents that efforts were being intensified to locate the abducted youths and secure their safe return. He also appealed to the families to remain calm and avoid taking actions capable of jeopardising the ongoing rescue efforts. The post Abducted NYSC Members: Parents accuse transport firm of withholding passengers’ next-of-kin details appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Élections du 23 septembre : le Parquet fait état de 403 plaintes
items.description: Le chef du pôle de l'action publique, du suivi de l’exécution de la politique pénale et de l'analyse du phénomène criminel à la Présidence du Ministère public, Mourad El Alami, a affirmé, vendredi, que les élections du 23 septembre 2026 se sont déroulées normalement et dans de bonnes conditions, soulignant que le nombre de plaintes enregistrées à l'occasion de ce scrutin (403 plaintes) a connu une baisse par rapport à celui enregistré lors des élections de 2021 (1.071 plaintes). M. El Alami a expliqué qu'en vertu de leurs attributions constitutionnelles, les Parquets ont reçu 403 plaintes, certaines ayant été déposées directement auprès des Parquets, tandis que d'autres ont été soumises par voie électronique via les applications informatiques mises en place par la Présidence du Ministère public au profit des citoyens, leur permettant ainsi de déposer à distance leurs plaintes. Il a également relevé que le jour du scrutin a connu l’enregistrement du plus grand nombre des plaintes. M. El Alami a, en outre, assuré que les enquêtes judiciaires diligentées à ce sujet ont été menées avec précision et efficience, ainsi qu'avec la célérité nécessaire requise lors de cette étape, le délai moyen de réalisation des enquêtes n’ayant pas dépassé pas les 48 heures. L'analyse de la nature des infractions électorales enregistrées au niveau des parquets démontre que la plupart concernent des crimes de droit commun commis habituellement dans le cadre des campagnes électorales, tels que les actes de violence, les échanges d’injures et d’insultes, ainsi que l'atteinte à la vie privée, a-t-il expliqué. M. El Alami a également souligné une augmentation du nombre de crimes commis via les moyens électroniques, à savoir les réseaux sociaux, où plusieurs plaintes enregistrées, dans ce cadre, concernent la diffamation ou la violation de la vie privée. Des enquêtes judiciaires ont été ouvertes à cet effet et des poursuites ont été engagées à l’encontre des contrevenants, a-t-il dit. Concernant les affaires de non-remise des copies des procès-verbaux aux délégués des candidats, elles sont restées limitées aussi bien en nombre que sur le plan géographique. Ainsi, a-t-il poursuivi, quatre plaintes ont été enregistrées, réparties entre les circonscriptions électorales locales de Guelmim, Fahs-Anjra et Souk El Arbaa du Gharb. Il a ainsi été procédé à l’ouverture des enquêtes judiciaires et à la prise des mesures juridiques nécessaires : deux plaintes ont été classées sans suite faute de preuve de l'acte criminel, alors que les deux autres sont toujours en cours d'investigation. M. El Alami a, par ailleurs, rappelé que la loi organique relative à la Chambre des représentants définit précisément, à travers l’article 57, la procédure adoptée pour l’obtention des copies de ces procès-verbaux, puisque les présidents des bureaux de vote remettent ces copies aux délégués des candidats présents lors de l’établissement de ces procès verbaux. Dans ce contexte, il a affirmé que ce crime lié à la non-remise des procès-verbaux de vote requiert une condition spécifique : la présence du délégué du candidat à l’intérieur du bureau de vote au moment de l’établissement du procès-verbal, ajoutant que si cette personne quitte le bureau pour y revenir ultérieurement après l’achèvement de l’opération de dépouillement et de l’établissement du procès-verbal du vote, les éléments juridiques constitutifs du crime ne se trouvent pas réunis et, par conséquent, il est impossible d'engager des poursuites judiciaires à ce sujet, faute de cette condition juridique fondamentale. Ainsi, le scrutin du 23 septembre a fait l'objet d'un accompagnement direct de la part des Parquets, à travers un suivi minutieux des étapes de cette échéance, une application stricte de la loi, et une volonté de garantir le déroulement de ces élections dans des conditions saines où sont respectées les règles juridiques encadrant cette opération. The post Élections du 23 septembre : le Parquet fait état de 403 plaintes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Svetlana Tijanóvskaya: “Si dejamos que Ucrania pierda la guerra, la pregunta será quién es el siguiente”
items.description: Durante cinco años, Svetlana Tijanóvskaya ha portado en cada aparición pública un retrato de su marido, Serguéi Tijanovski, que era el candidato opositor en las elecciones de 2020 pero fue encarcelado antes de la votación. Entonces fue ella la que encabezó la lista, en medio de una movilización masiva, en unos comicios en los que el presidente, Alexandr Lukashenko, se proclamó ganador con un increíble 80% de los votos. Siguieron manifestaciones multitudinarias contra el fraude y una brutal represión, y Tijanóvskaya tuvo que refugiarse en Lituania , donde montó una precaria estructura de Gobierno en el exilio. Su marido fue liberado el pasado verano, junto a unos 500 opositores más, pero ella apareció este sábado en el Foro La Toja Vínculo Atlántico, en Pontevedra, con otro retrato de un hombre en la mano. Y explicó que cada día elige uno de los más de 900 rostros de presos políticos que siguen en las cárceles de Lukashenko. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Sport/CAP Rugby : Les formateurs togolais bénéficient d’un suivi pédagogique à Lomé
items.description: Lomé, 2 oct. (ATOP) – Trois formateurs arbitres et trois entraîneurs togolais ayant participé à la première formation du projet « Collectif Afrique Pacifique Rugby (CAP Rugby) », tenue en Côte d’Ivoire en 2025, bénéficient depuis le vendredi 2 octobre à Lomé d’un suivi pédagogique de leurs acquis. Prévu pour trois jours, ce suivi vise à renforcer les compétences des acteurs formés et à contribuer au développement du rugby, tout en favorisant son utilisation comme outil de développement. M. Ndaw (T-shirt blanc au fonds) expliquant le projet Les travaux sont conduits par trois formateurs de la Fédération française de rugby (FFR), sous la direction du chef de projet « CAP Rugby », Malick Ndaw. Les entraîneurs seront notamment évalués sur les fondamentaux du rugby, à travers des exercices pratiques portant sur le rugby sans contact, la mêlée, le plaquage, le jeu au pied et le toucher. La formation aborde également les dimensions physique, technique, tactique et mentale de la pratique sportive. Les participants travailleront notamment sur l’endurance, la force, la vitesse, la souplesse, les passes, le jeu au pied, la lecture du jeu, la prise de décision, la concentration et l’esprit d’équipe. L’hygiène de vie de l’athlète, notamment le sommeil, l’alimentation et la récupération, fait également partie des enseignements. Les arbitres seront, pour leur part, suivis sur plusieurs modules, notamment le hors-jeu et les enjeux dans le jeu courant, le plaquage, la mêlée et l’avantage. A l’issue de ce processus, les arbitres formés dans le cadre du projet auront pour mission de contribuer à la formation de huit nouveaux arbitres de la Fédération togolaise de rugby (FTR). Malick Ndaw a expliqué que le projet repose sur deux axes : développer le rugby à travers la formation des formateurs d’entraîneurs et d’arbitres, et faire de cette discipline un véritable outil de développement. Financé par l’Agence française de développement (AFD) et mis en œuvre par Expertise France, en partenariat avec la Fédération française de rugby, le projet CAP Rugby couvre 15 pays d’Afrique et du Pacifique. Il vise à renforcer le développement du rugby à travers la formation et l’accompagnement des acteurs du secteur, notamment les administrateurs, les formateurs d’entraîneurs et les formateurs d’arbitres. Le « Tournoi Rugby O’Féminin » lancé Par ailleurs, le suivi pédagogique a également servi de cadre au lancement du « Tournoi Rugby O’Féminin », porté par la Fédération togolaise de rugby avec l’appui financier de CAP Rugby. D’une durée de trois mois, ce projet concerne le Lycée de Togblékopé et le Lycée de Cacavelli. Quatre enseignants d’éducation physique et sportive (EPS) et six éducateurs de la FTR seront formés par les trois entraîneurs togolais ayant participé à la formation CAP Rugby. Ils interviendront ensuite dans les deux établissements pour initier les jeunes filles à la pratique du rugby. Un tournoi réunissant les deux lycées est prévu en décembre. Le projet ambitionne de créer six équipes de rugby féminin, soit trois dans chacun d’eux. Ce choix s’explique par le fait que ces structures ont déjà accueilli le programme « Get Into Rugby », destiné aux jeunes filles et garçons. Les élèves maîtrisent ainsi les bases de la discipline, ce qui devrait faciliter la mise en œuvre du nouveau projet. « Ce projet est motivé par un diagnostic selon lequel nous n’avons pas assez de clubs de rugby féminin au Togo. Nous avons donc trouvé que cette initiative permettrait d’amener le rugby à la base, à l’école, et d’avoir six nouveaux clubs de rugby féminin », a indiqué la coordonnatrice, Gadégbéku Cécile. items.title: UAE investigators say flydubai co-pilot was planning 'terrorist act'
items.description: The United Arab Emirates’ attorney general said the co-pilot of a flydubai flight to Israel had planned a “terrorist act” and used the cockpit’s emergency axe to attack the captain, the official UAE news agency WAM reported on Saturday. The news agency quoted Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi as saying that according to the initial findings of an investigation , “the co-pilot had attempted to carry out a terrorist act” and had “attacked the captain in the cockpit with the emergency axe and tried to take control of the aircraft”. Separately, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who had earlier showered the Indian captain with praise for saving the plane, invited him to Israel as a guest of honour. “You are a true hero of the brave peoples of India and Israel and you are a hero of the entire world,” Netanyahu said in a video his office released of his telephone conversation with Captain Smit Machchhar. UAE Deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed, also the country’s defence minister and the crown prince of Dubai, visited Smit at a hospital. In a post on X, he described him as the “pilot who embodied the highest degrees of courage, responsibility, and care for human life”. The defence minister added: “From us, and from the leadership of the nation, he has our full appreciation and praise. “We are proud that he is part of our team… part of the story of our nation… and part of what the UAE stands for… a nation of compassion… a nation of peace… and a nation of life.” Barred from flying The co-pilot accused of attacking the captain of a flydubai flight to Israel had previously been barred from flying in Oman over concerns about his extremist views, multiple media outlets reported. Scrutiny into the alleged assailant — who was identified in the reports as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami — and his motives has intensified after Wednesday’s drama aboard a Dubai-Tel Aviv route that officials say narrowly avoided catastrophe. During the flydubai flight, the jet’s Indian captain was assaulted by his co-pilot but he managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to overpower the attacker and force an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday that Omani authorities had banned the pilot from flying over concerns he had adopted radical ideological views, citing people familiar with the matter. CNN , citing two sources familiar with the matter, reported the pilot was removed from a job at Oman’s national airline last year over concerns about extremist views. Al Arabiya , citing an informed source, reported that Omani authorities determined that the co-pilot held extremist views. The broadcaster said he had also spent time in Syria, raising concerns he may have been influenced by radical groups there. ABC News , citing senior intelligence and law enforcement officials familiar with the investigation, reported the suspect had allegedly been found in possession of extremist materials while he was a trainee.

items.title: Ghana gaining notoriety for drugs – Bawumia demands bipartisan probe
items.description: Former Vice President and NPP Presidential Candidate, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has raised alarm over what he says is Ghana’s growing international notoriety for drug trafficking, accusing the NDC government of responding with mere meetings instead of decisive action. Addressing the NPP National Delegates Conference in Kumasi, the 2028 flagbearer said Ghana’s name is being dragged through the ports of Europe as drugs pass through Ghana’s borders unnoticed. “Our dear motherland is gaining notoriety for drugs being arrested abroad, having passed through our borders unnoticed. Our country’s name is being dragged through the ports of Europe, and the government has answered with meetings, not results,” he said. He called for a bipartisan committee of Parliament, sitting in public, with powers to summon witnesses and demand shipping records. “Arresting couriers is not enough. Ghanaians want to know who is financing these shipments and how they keep getting through. As many religious groups, civil society organisations and concerned Ghanaians have expressed, this is ruining the international image of our country and we must act now,” he stressed. On galamsey, Dr Bawumia was candid. “Let us be honest. Galamsey has troubled almost every government in the Fourth Republic. It is a complex national challenge that demands seriousness, not slogans,” he said. He accused the NDC of making unrealistic promises to end galamsey in months and restore polluted water bodies. “Ghanaians are reminded every day of how the NDC and its senior officials, many of whom are Cabinet Ministers and top CEOs today, lambasted the NPP government and told Ghanaians that they possessed the magic to end galamsey instantly if voted into office. Today, under their watch, in nearly two years, galamsey has grown embarrassingly worse,” he noted. He also turned to education and health. He said Agenda 111, designed to provide district hospitals, has stalled under the NDC, denying millions access to healthcare and health graduates jobs. On Free SHS, he said the programme is suffering after the NDC promised to improve it. “After they promised to improve meals for students, today it has deteriorated. Many of our young BECE graduates are being deliberately cut off from Free SHS, and what frustrated parents are told by the government is that their wards have deservedly failed,” he said. He reminded delegates and the nation that the NDC never believed in Free SHS and bastardised it for years until they saw its impact. On cocoa and other promises, he said: “The promises to cocoa farmers to increase the cocoa price to GHC 6,500 have turned out to be a scam. The promise of automatic posting of teachers and nurses… has turned out to be another scam. Even their much-touted Nkoko Nkitikiti programme has failed.”

items.title: Government urges SMEs to embrace digitalisation for growth and job creation
items.description: The Government has urged Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) to adopt digital technologies and innovation to improve productivity, reduce operational waste and create more employment opportunities. Noah Tumfo, the Chief Director of the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, said SMEs remained critical to Ghana’s economic development, particularly as unemployment put pressure on the formal sector. He said the government was focused on creating the right policy and regulatory environment to enable entrepreneurs to innovate, expand their businesses and create sustainable jobs. “SMEs are the backbone of our development. If SMEs grow, the country benefits,” Mr Tumfo said. He was speaking at an SME awards programme aimed at recognising entrepreneurs and motivating them to expand their businesses and contribute to economic productivity. Mr Tumfo said digitalisation was becoming an important tool for helping SMEs identify operational challenges and improve efficiency. He cited a recently completed project implemented by the Ministry in collaboration with the United Nations Industrial Development Organisation (UNIDO) and the Government of Japan, which helped SMEs use technology to identify challenges on their shop floors and develop targeted solutions. He said such interventions could help businesses reduce waste and focus more resources on increasing their productive capacity. “We are looking to have more of such situations where digitalisation becomes a norm because it helps SMEs to cut down their waste and focus more on expanding their productivity base for the benefit of the country,” he said. The Chief Director said the Ghana Enterprises Agency (GEA) was the main government institution responsible for providing direct support to SMEs through training, grants, funding opportunities and soft loans. He explained that while the Ministry provided the policy and regulatory framework, its agencies supported businesses with the practical interventions needed to overcome operational challenges. Mr Tumfo said the ultimate objective was to help Ghanaian SMEs grow beyond the domestic market and compete internationally. He said expanding into international markets would enable businesses to generate foreign exchange and contribute more significantly to the national economy. Mr Tumfo therefore urged entrepreneurs to see recognition through SME awards as a motivation to improve their businesses, create more jobs and increase productivity. Mr Kwesi Ofori Jnr, the Executive Director and Co-founder of SME Grow Africa (SMEGA), said SMEs also needed to strengthen their business structures and capacity to attract investment and access international markets. He said SMEGA had, since 2013, worked with SMEs to identify suitable partners, improve their business positioning, access training and connect with investors and new markets. He stated that the organisation had facilitated market and investment opportunities for businesses across Africa, Europe and Asia. Mr Ofori Jnr. said beneficiaries of the initiative would have access to masterclasses, capacity-building programmes and opportunities to engage international investors. He said the ability of SMEs to attract investment depended largely on how well they were structured and positioned to demonstrate their potential to prospective partners. “Beyond recognition, it is important that we set them on the right path,” he said, and encouraged SMEs to consider business insurance, environmental sustainability and good corporate practices as they expanded. He said businesses needed to adopt environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles and ensure that their operations were sustainable. He further urged business owners to develop proper succession plans to ensure that their companies survived beyond their founders. He said SMEs that invested in capacity building, sound business structures, partnerships, and sustainable practices would be better positioned to expand and contribute to Ghana’s economic development.

items.title: Ghana’s university libraries urged to lead change in digital age
items.description: Ghana’s university libraries must do more than preserve books and provide access to information if they are to remain central to teaching, research and learning in a rapidly changing academic environment, senior university leaders and librarians have said. They say the growing influence of digital technology, artificial intelligence, open access and changing expectations from students and researchers requires academic libraries to rethink their traditional role. The call was made at the 42nd Annual General Meeting and Conference of University Librarians Ghana (ULG), hosted by the University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development (USTED) in Kumasi from 30 September to 1 October 2026. The conference brought together university librarians, researchers and higher-education leaders under the theme: “Leading the Change: Developing Resilient Library Leaders for a Transforming Academic Landscape.” The programme included discussions on open access, research communication and widening public access to knowledge. For Professor Isaac Boateng, Pro-Vice Chancellor of USTED, the challenge facing libraries is not simply how to acquire new technology, but how to adapt it intelligently to local circumstances. “Change is already here. The question is not whether our libraries will change. They must. The real question is whether we will lead the change or merely respond to it,” he told the gathering. Professor Boateng argued that the explosion of information made the role of libraries more important, rather than less important. The challenge, he said, was increasingly about helping people distinguish between information, knowledge, understanding and wisdom. “The library of the future cannot simply be a place where information is stored. It must be a place where knowledge is trusted, ideas are cultivated, scholarship is protected and minds are liberated,” he said. He said libraries needed leaders who understood emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, while remaining committed to intellectual freedom, academic integrity and the human purpose of education. For him, digital transformation should not mean simply copying models developed elsewhere. He used Ghana’s supermarket industry to illustrate his point. He contrasted the fortunes of Laba and Melcom, arguing that businesses that adapt to changing environments are better placed to remain relevant. He also pointed to the different approaches taken by Shoprite and Game when they entered Ghana’s retail market. The lesson, he said, was applicable to university libraries. “Can we simply do everything that European or Western libraries are doing and expect our institutions to survive and thrive? Probably not. We need to adapt,” he stated. That adaptation, he said, should include bringing local content into the digital environment and ensuring that libraries respond to the needs of Ghanaian students, researchers, academics and communities. The library as the university’s memory Professor Boateng warned that institutions that refuse to evolve could eventually become “museums of their own past”. Universities are changing, he said, while students, researchers, technology and the economics of higher education are also changing. “Therefore, library leadership must change as well,” he said. But he stressed that change alone was not enough. Libraries also needed resilience, the ability to respond to disruption without abandoning their professional identity or purpose. He described resilient leaders as people who could turn challenges into opportunities to innovate. “Leadership is not about occupying an office. Leadership is about creating a future that is better than the present,” he said. He called for a new generation of library leaders who could become “architects of knowledge ecosystems” rather than simply administrators of collections. Such leaders, he said, should understand artificial intelligence and its ethical implications, promote open access while protecting quality and academic integrity, and understand data without losing sight of the people represented by it. “The library is central to the university’s intellectual mission,” he said. Making knowledge more accessible For Dr Theresa Adu, University Librarian at the University of Health and Allied Sciences, collaboration among academic libraries is essential because many of the resources required for teaching, learning and research are expensive. She said University Librarians Ghana works closely with the Consortium of Academic and Research Libraries in Ghana, which helps universities obtain electronic resources through collective arrangements. “Electronic resources are very expensive, yet teaching, learning and research depend heavily on access to resources,” she said. According to Dr Adu, collaboration has helped make electronic resources available across Ghana’s university system at a more affordable cost to participating institutions. But she said the direction of travel should go further, towards open science, open access and Open Educational Resources. “Without access to information, there is no future,” she said. Open access, she explained, can help remove some of the barriers created when academic information is placed behind paywalls. Open Educational Resources can also provide teaching and learning materials to lecturers and students without requiring institutions or individuals to purchase every resource. Showing the value of libraries Dr Adu said another issue requiring attention was the visibility of the work librarians do. Libraries contribute significantly to universities, she said, but much of that work is not always visible to the wider public. She cited an African proverb about the lizard that falls from a high iroko tree and praises itself when nobody else does. Her message was that librarians must be prepared to demonstrate their impact. “If we do not tell people about our work and its impact, nobody else will do it for us,” she said. That, she suggested, means libraries need to communicate more clearly how their services contribute to research, teaching, learning and the wider academic mission. Succession planning was another concern raised by Dr Adu. She said academic librarians needed to identify and develop future leaders before existing leaders moved on. The presence of new faces at professional gatherings, she said, was a reminder that people were constantly moving through and out of different positions. As they do, new leaders must be ready to take over. “These new leaders should not simply come in without knowing what to do. They must be properly prepared, equipped with the necessary skills and knowledge, and able to perform their responsibilities effectively,” she said. Resilience beyond the library Chairman of University Librarians Ghana and University Librarian at USTED, Dr Christopher M. Owusu-Ansah, said the conference was an opportunity for the professional body to examine its work, identify weaknesses and plan for the future. “We put up this meeting to evaluate our activities,” he said. The organisation brings together university librarians from Ghana’s public universities, including traditional and technical universities. Dr Owusu-Ansah said the conference was intended to leave members with a renewed sense of purpose and a stronger capacity to withstand challenges. “We want them to return with a resilient mentality and attitude — one that does not yield in the face of challenges,” he said. He said challenges were inevitable, but librarians had the capacity to overcome them. The experience of the Covid-19 pandemic, he noted, had demonstrated the importance of university libraries to academic continuity. When teaching and learning moved online, libraries continued providing resources that supported teaching, learning and research. “We expect our members to go back and do even more,” he said. But resilience, he argued, should not be limited to institutional performance. University librarians also need to pay attention to their physical and mental wellbeing, financial planning, budgeting and strategic management. The objective, he said, was to ensure that the libraries they lead could continue to function and that their staff were empowered to contribute to the wider mandates of their universities. Leading rather than following The discussions point to a changing understanding of what an academic library should be. It is no longer enough to ask how many books are on a shelf or how many electronic databases a university can access. The bigger questions concern how libraries help universities navigate an age of information abundance, digital disruption and rapidly changing research practices. Professor Boateng said the future would ultimately depend less on the technologies libraries adopt than on how intelligently they adapt those technologies to their own circumstances. The responsibility, he said, also extends beyond individual institutions. University libraries are custodians of Ghana’s intellectual heritage, facilitators of research and partners in teaching and learning. They are also increasingly being called upon to help protect the integrity of knowledge at a time when the volume of information available to the public is expanding rapidly. “The future of our libraries will not be determined simply by the technologies we adopt. It will be determined by how intelligently we adapt them to our context, how effectively we protect our values, and how courageously we lead our institutions through change,” he said.

items.title: « Une question de souveraineté » : Tebboune répond au FMI sur les réserves de change
items.description: Avant son commentaire ce samedi sur les prévisions du FMI , le président de la République Abdelmadjid Tebboune avait évoqué les réserves de change de l’Algérie dans son discours devant les deux chambres du Parlement en décembre dernier. Il avait indiqué que les avoirs extérieurs du pays étaient à un « niveau acceptable », couvrant les importations du pays pour une durée de près d'une année et demie. Les réserves de change de l'Algérie étaient estimées à 69 milliards de dollars en 2024 et 51 milliards en 2025. Réserves de change : ternes prévisions du FMI Dans son dernier rapport publié le 21 septembre dernier, le Fonds monétaire international prévoit une chute drastique des réserves de l’Algérie à 19,8 milliards de dollars à l’horizon 2031 contre 46,5 milliards de dollars en 2026. Deux facteurs principaux déterminent l’évolution des réserves de change de l’Algérie : le niveau des exportations et celui des importations. L’essentiel des recettes d’exportation de l’Algérie étant tiré des hydrocarbures, les cours du pétrole et du gaz sont donc déterminants dans le calcul des prévisions des réserves. Le FMI a basé ses calculs sur l’évolution des importations et les prévisions des cours du pétrole dans les années à venir. Or, l’Algérie a entamé un chantier ambitieux de diversification de son économie avec l’objectif de réduire la dépendance aux recettes des exportations d’hydrocarbures. Tebboune sur les réserves de change : « Une question de souveraineté » Dans sa rencontre périodique avec des médias nationaux, dont des extraits ont été diffusés ce samedi 3 octobre, le président Tebboune a démenti les prévisions du FMI en rappelant que l'Algérie est résolument engagée dans la diversification de ses ressources. « Nous travaillons pour augmenter nos revenus hors hydrocarbures. Ce n’est pas une question de devises. C’est une question de souveraineté », a répondu le chef de l’État à une question sur la fonte du matelas des réserves de change annoncée par le FMI. Il est vrai que, jusque-là, l’essentiel des recettes en devises est assuré par les exportations de gaz et de pétrole. Mais depuis quelques années, les exportations hors hydrocarbures commencent à bouger, atteignant en 2022 plus de 6 milliards de dollars, alors qu'elles peinaient à dépasser le milliard de dollars les années précédentes. Pour l’année 2026, les prévisions tablent sur 7,8 milliards de dollars. Des projets qui exporteront ou qui vont se substituer aux importations La véritable percée des exportations algériennes d’hydrocarbures est attendue dans quelques années, lorsque les grands projets structurants entreront en phase de production et d’exportation. Les plus notables sont les projets d’exploitation des gisements de fer de Gara Djebilet, de phosphate à Tébessa et de zinc et plomb à Béjaïa. Parallèlement, le tissu industriel se diversifie d’année en année et d’autres grands projets structurants sont lancés dans l’agriculture, comme la ferme géante Baladna à Adrar, ou encore le projet céréalier avec l'Italien BF à Timimoun. L'Algérie ambitionne, en outre, de porter sa production de céréales à moyen terme à 9 millions de tonnes, couvrant une large part de ses besoins. Même dans le cas où ils n’exporteraient pas, ces projets contribueront à renflouer les réserves de change en se substituant aux importations. Le projet Baladna est illustratif. La ferme de 270.000 vaches devrait alimenter une usine qui produira 193.000 tonnes de poudre de lait. Un produit que l'Algérie importe actuellement pour une facture de 600 millions de dollars par an. L’article « Une question de souveraineté » : Tebboune répond au FMI sur les réserves de change est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: NPP National Delegates Conference: Nhyiaeso MP calls for unity and peace
items.description: Member of Parliament for Nhyiaeso, Stephen Amoah, has called on members of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) to prioritise unity and peace as the party holds its National Delegates Conference in Kumasi. Speaking at the conference on Saturday, 3 October, Mr Amoah said the most important consideration for delegates should be the election of national executives who have the competence and leadership qualities required to help the party win its next election. “I expect that we get a set of national executives that can actually help us to win the elections. I think that’s the most important thing,” he said. He emphasised that the party needs competent national executives with what it takes to develop an effective strategy to win power from the NDC. According to him, the NPP’s ultimate objective should remain its return to government, choosing national executives a critical decision for delegates at the conference. Mr Amoah, however, stressed that the leadership contest should not undermine the unity of the party or create divisions among its members. He urged delegates and other party members to ensure that the conference is conducted peacefully, saying unity should remain a fundamental principle throughout the process. “I also expect that the most important fundamental elements of unity will prevail here in peace,” he said. His comments come at a significant moment for the NPP as delegates gather to elect national executives who will take responsibility for leading the party and shaping its direction ahead of the next general election. For Mr Amoah, the leadership elections should therefore be viewed beyond individual ambitions, with the broader interests and electoral prospects of the party remaining central to the process. He said the NPP needs a leadership team capable of working towards the common objective of winning power, while ensuring that the process of selecting those leaders does not damage the cohesion of the party.

items.title: Cargill Ghana renovates, equips ICT laboratory for Ahmadiyya Basic School
items.description: Cargill Ghana Limited, through its Cargill Cares initiative, has renovated and equipped an Information and Communication Technology (ICT) laboratory at the Ahmadiyya Basic School in Tema to support digital education and skills development. The project involved the conversion of an existing classroom into a modern ICT laboratory equipped with 32 computers and monitors, a printer, 20 computer tables, 40 chairs, air-conditioning units, security doors, a television and internet connectivity. Speaking at the handover ceremony, Managing Director of Cargill Ghana Limited, Max Essoh Latte, said the investment forms part of the company’s commitment to creating opportunities for young people through education. “At Cargill, we believe that education is one of the most powerful ways to create opportunities and build stronger communities. By providing students with access to technology and a modern learning environment, we hope this facility will inspire them to develop the digital skills they need to succeed in an increasingly technology-driven world.” Mr Latte said the project was made possible through collaboration with the school and relevant education stakeholders, adding that the company was pleased to contribute to the development of young people in the Tema community. The Municipal Director of Education, Sophia Ako, commended Cargill Ghana for the initiative, stressing the importance of private-sector partnerships in improving educational outcomes. A representative of the Head of the Ahmadiyya Mission, Adam Kofi Yamoah, also expressed appreciation to Cargill Ghana, saying the facility would improve students’ and teachers’ access to technology and support teaching and learning. The handover ceremony brought together representatives of Cargill Ghana, the Ghana Education Service, the Ahmadiyya Mission, school leadership, teachers, students and other stakeholders. The newly renovated laboratory is expected to provide students and teachers with access to digital tools and internet-based learning resources while strengthening the school’s capacity to deliver ICT education.

items.title: GH¢6,500 cocoa promise has turned out to be a scam – Bawumia
items.description: New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has criticised the Mahama administration for not fulfilling its promises to cocoa farmers. Speaking at the NPP’s National Delegates Conference at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium on Saturday, October 3, Dr Bawumia said the government’s promise to increase the producer price of cocoa to GH¢6,500 had not been delivered. “The promises to cocoa farmers to increase the cocoa price to GH¢6,500 has turned out to be a scam,” Dr Bawumia said. He also criticised the government over its promises to introduce automatic posting for teachers and nurses and improve their conditions of service. “The promise of automatic posting of teachers and nurses and the improvement in their conditions of service has turned out to be another scam,” he said. Dr Bawumia further accused the government of failing to fulfil its promise to cancel the teacher licensure examinations and to pay customers affected by the collapse of Menzgold and other financial institutions. “The promise to cancel teacher licensure examinations has proven to be another scam, just as the promise to pay all Menzgold customers and customers of all financial institutions which collapsed,” he said. He added that the government’s much-touted Nkoko Nkitikiti programme had also failed to meet expectations. Dr Bawumia described the issues as part of what he called the record of the NDC government after two years in office. “This is the record of the NDC two years on. As our elders say, ‘Agoro no be so a na afri anopa’. Ghana deserves better,” he said. He assured supporters that an NPP government, if elected in 2029, would draw lessons from its previous administration, including both its successes and challenges, to improve governance. “I assure you that when the NPP assumes the reins of office in 2029, by the grace of God, we shall bring to bear the lessons of our successes and challenges to do a way better job in these and other areas than this NDC government is doing,” Dr Bawumia said.

items.title: Santé : le navire-hôpital chinois Auspicious Ark accoste à Conakry pour une semaine de soins gratuits
items.description: Comme nous l'annoncions, le navire-hôpital chinois Auspicious Ark a accosté, ce samedi 3 octobre 2026, au Port autonome de Conakry, pour sa deuxième escale en Guinée. L’imposant bateau a été accosté aux environs de 10 heures. À leur arrivée, les membres de l’équipage, composés notamment de médecins chinois, de militaires et de l’ensemble du personnel, ont été accueillis par l’ambassadeur de la République populaire de Chine en République de Guinée, entouré de ressortissants chinois ainsi que d’officiers supérieurs des Forces de défense et de sécurité guinéennes. Pendant une semaine, du 3 au 10 octobre 2026, des milliers de Guinéens, préalablement sélectionnés, bénéficieront gratuitement de consultations médicales et de soins. Selon les informations fournies par un membre du personnel du navire, jusqu’à 600 consultations sont prévues chaque jour. À l’occasion d’une visite guidée réservée aux médias, dont Mediaguinée, nous avons découvert plusieurs installations de cet hôpital flottant, notamment la salle d’accueil, la salle de réanimation, le service d’imagerie médicale équipé d’un scanner de haute technologie, le service de radiographie, la salle d’observation, les salles de consultations externes, le laboratoire médical, les unités de diagnostic de l’hépatite B et du VIH, le service d’échographie, le cabinet dentaire doté d’une salle de radiologie dentaire, le département de médecine traditionnelle chinoise ainsi que le service d’ophtalmologie. À l’issue de cette visite de l’hôpital mobile, le médecin-colonel Abdel Kémoko Diallo a annoncé la tenue d’une réunion technique entre les médecins chinois, le personnel du Service de Santé des Armées et celui du ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique, avant l’acheminement des premiers patients vers le navire. « Demain matin à 6 heures, le personnel du Service de Santé des Armées se rendra au Stade de la Mission pour acheminer les premiers qui ont été appelés. pour être ici. Arrivés ici, il y aura la symbiose de l'équipe médicale chinoise et de l'équipe médicale militaire pour le choix de ceux-là qui doivent être consultés et ceux-là qui doivent être hospitalisés pour les différentes interventions chirurgicales », a-t-il expliqué. Poursuivant son intervention, le médecin-colonel Abdel Kémoko Diallo est revenu sur les modalités de prise en charge ainsi que sur les différentes pathologies concernées par cette mission médicale. « Je ne vais pas vous dire toutes les pathologies qui doivent être prises en charge. D'abord, avant une intervention, il faut un bilan préopératoire. Ces patients, avant d'être là, doivent venir avec les bulletins d'examens et les résultats. En fonction de ces résultats, les patients-là doivent être hospitalisés. Pour les différentes interventions, je peux vous dire ici, pratiquement à part le côté traumato, il y a toutes sortes d'interventions, à commencer par l'ophtalmo, les cas de cataracte, les cas d'appendicite, les cas d'hernie, même au niveau de la gynécologie, les cas de grossesse, certainement par la césarienne ou par la voie basse, l'accouchement. Il y aura même la médecine traditionnelle chinoise qui sera appliquée sur les patients », a-t-il précisé. En conclusion, le général de division Mamadou Aliou Sow, président du comité technique de défense et de sécurité et porte-parole du ministère de la Défense nationale, s’est dit rassuré quant à la qualité des soins qui seront reçus à bord de ce navire-hôpital. « Je voudrais apprécier le niveau de performance des appareils qu'on a visités et les scanners à tous les niveaux, et la propreté qui y sied à l'intérieur du bateau. On est rassuré. Parce que quand quelqu'un est malade et va dans un service de santé propre, bien équipé, la santé vient déjà ». Mamadou Yaya Barry & Robert Kourouma L’article Santé : le navire-hôpital chinois Auspicious Ark accoste à Conakry pour une semaine de soins gratuits est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Pakistan summons Indian envoy over killing of 2 civilians by border troops
items.description: Pakistan summoned the Indian chargé d’affaires to lodge a strong protest over the killing of two Pakistani civilians by Indian Border Security Force (BSF) personnel in the Bedian sector along the international border, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday. Two unarmed Pakistani civilians were martyred and another was injured in firing by India’s BSF near the border in Kasur on Friday. “The BSF personnel resorted to unprovoked and lethal force against unarmed civilians. Such use of force was wholly unjustified and grossly disproportionate, resulting in the tragic loss of two precious lives,” the FO said. Pakistan categorically rejects any attempt to mischaracterise the deceased as “infiltrators”, it added. The FO said the incident constituted a serious violation of fundamental human rights, including the right to life, and raised concerns over the protection of civilian life under international law. It called on the Indian side to “conduct an immediate, transparent and credible investigation”, take appropriate disciplinary and legal action against those responsible, and formally communicate the findings and action taken to the government of Pakistan. India was further urged to “respect fundamental human rights and international law, strictly observe relevant bilateral arrangements and established border procedures, exercise maximum restraint in such situations, and take effective measures to prevent similar incidents in the future”, the FO said. Across the border, India’s foreign ministry said it had summoned the chargé d’affaires of the Pakistan High Commission to protest what it alleged was the “continued facilitation of illegal cross-border infiltration from Pakistan”. The three civilians were residents of Ladhar village and had moved a few steps ahead of a border pillar when the BSF opened fire on them without warning. All three were unarmed. The deceased were identified as Azmat Rasool and Mohsin Jutt, both residents of Jattan Wali Haveli, Ladhar. The injured civilian was taken for medical treatment. According to security sources, none of the three men had attempted to cross the border fence, with the incident described as a violation of the border agreement and standard operating procedures governing the international border. The development comes a day after Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry lampooned India’s claims of “neutralising” a “terrorist” allegedly linked to the Pakistani military, presenting the individual during a press conference. Asked whether the recent allegations could trigger another armed conflict between the neighbours during the press briefing, he affirmed that Pakistan’s armed forces were always ready for any such move and warned of “very harsh” retribution. Additional input from Reuters

items.title: ONSR | Hausse marquée des décès sur les routes depuis janvier 2026
items.description: L'Observatoire national de la sécurité routière (ONSR) a publié un récent bilan faisant état d'une baisse du nombre d'accidents de la circulation depuis le début de l'année, malgré une hausse marquée de la mortalité sur les routes. Selon les données communiquées par l'ONSR, 3 616 accidents de la route ont été enregistrés depuis le début de l'année, causant 1029 décès et faisant 4692 blessés, contre 4177 accidents, 929 morts et 5534 blessés l'année dernière durant la même période. Bien que le nombre total d'accidents soit en baisse, la gravité de ces derniers s'est accentuée, se traduisant par une hausse du nombre de victimes mortelles, révèle ledit bilan. Parmi les multiples facteurs à l'origine de ces drames, l'ONST cite l'inattention et la distraction au volant occupant la première place. Elles sont directement impliquées dans 1112 accidents, soit 30,75 % du total des drames de la route enregistrés cette année. Les autorités de la circulation ont par ailleurs réitéré leurs appels à la vigilance, au respect du code de la route et à l'évitement de toute source de distraction au volant. Y. N. items.title: We’ll pursue accountability despite intimidation – Afenyo-Markin
items.description: Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has accused the Mahama government of trying to frighten and silence its critics, saying the minority will continue to demand accountability. Speaking at the NPP’s National Delegates Congress in Kumasi on Saturday, 3 October, Mr Afenyo-Markin said critics of the government should be allowed to express their views without fear of arrest or imprisonment. Afenyo-Markin said the government’s actions were aimed at intimidating critics, arguing that the previous Akufo-Addo administration endured harsher criticism. “Critics are arrested and jailed for saying things the NDC government doesn’t like. Under Akufo-Addo, we heard worse things against Akufo-Addo, but we endured,” he said. Mr Afenyo-Markin said the NPP would continue to use democratic and parliamentary processes to scrutinise the government’s decisions, insisting that the opposition would not be intimidated. “We will defend our freedoms and pursue accountability through democratic means. We, the Minority, shall never be intimidated in Parliament; we will fight for you till we gain power in 2028. They want critics tired, afraid,” he said. He subsequently called on members of the NPP and the Minority to be more assertive in challenging government policies and decisions. “Let’s hold the government accountable without fear of arrest and intimidation,” he said, stressing that the opposition had a responsibility to scrutinise the administration on behalf of the electorate. Call for party unity The Minority Leader also used his address to rally NPP members around the party’s reorganisation and its preparations for the 2028 general election. He described the party’s presidential candidate, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, as “a doer and problem solver” and urged party members to unite behind the leadership as the NPP seeks to rebuild after its return to opposition. Mr Afenyo-Markin expressed confidence in the party’s prospects, telling supporters: “The Lord is with us; come 2028, we shall prevail.” Kufuor urges careful choice of party leaders Former President John Agyekum Kufuor also addressed the congress through a video message, calling on delegates to carefully consider the qualities required of the party’s next generation of national leaders. Mr Kufuor said Ghana needed the NPP to contribute to the country’s pursuit of prosperity and transformation. “Ghana needs NPP to lead to prosperity and transformation,” he said. He urged delegates selecting the new national executive committee to focus on leadership capable of restoring public confidence in the party. He also invoked the principle of popular sovereignty, calling on the party to demonstrate “true respect for the idea that true sovereignty is with the people”. Akufo-Addo backs Bawumia for 2028 Former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo also addressed the gathering, expressing confidence that the NPP could return to government in 2028 under Dr Bawumia. “With God’s guidance, we will emerge victorious as we did in 2000 and 2016 and form the government in 2028 with Dr Bawumia,” he said. The positions include National Chairman, Vice Chairman, General Secretary, National Organiser, National Women’s Organiser, National Youth Organiser, National Nasara Organiser, National Treasurer and National Communications Director.

items.title: Local automakers voice concerns as imports of used cars surge in Sept
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Imports of used cars surged in September after easing of regulations, inviting criticism from local manufacturers while importers claim that the move will bring competition in the auto sector. After a brief decline due to the government abolishing the Pers­onal Baggage Scheme and applying restrictions to control misuse of used car schemes for overseas Pakistanis, imports of used cars have started surging again. In the month of September, a total of 2,276 vehicles were imported under the Gift Scheme as the strict restrictions under the Baggage Scheme continue, according to data from the Commerce Ministry. The figures show that in May, only 48 used cars were imported mainly through the baggage scheme. However, the situation started to change from June onwards. In June, a total of 843 vehicles were imported, including 806 under the Gift Scheme. The figure reached 1,938 in July, with 1,876 cars under the Gift Scheme. August saw a total of 1,445 vehicle imports, while 2,276 vehicles were imported in September, with 2,238 under the Gift Scheme. A senior executive of the auto industry noted that the reduction in duties on completely built units (CBUs) by 20-25 per cent in the 2026-27 budget has reduced the import cost. “We have reports that a one-year restriction on transfer of ownership is not being implemented in some cities, due to which this business is flourishing again, but at the cost of the domestic auto industry which consists of 13 assemblers and over 300 auto parts manufacturers,” the executive added. Auto parts vendors expressed their concerns too, claiming that auto production had finally begun to show an increase after a gap of three years, which was also contributing to Pakistan’s growth in the large-scale manufacturing (LSM) sector . “Locally produced cars contain up to 60pc local parts by value, amounting to an average of Rs1.5 million per vehicle, and import of 2,276 used vehicles meant loss of Rs3.4 billion of local parts production which creates jobs and operates in the documented economy,” said Abdul Rehman Aizaz, chairman of Pakistan Asso­ciation of Automotive Parts and Ac­­cessories Manufacturers (Paa­pam). He termed it unfair that, on the one hand, the proposed auto policy was slashing import duties on new cars, while on the other hand, imports of used cars were being encouraged. “Ultimately, Pakistan is moving towards a market dominated by imported new and used vehicles with no industrial activity,” the Paapam chairman said, terming the business of used cars completely unregulated. Competition in auto sector On the contrary, importers claim that Pakistan needs to have a competitive economy and that importing used cars was completely legal if done as per the government regulations. “Currently, all imported vehicles are subjected to pre-shipment inspections by the accredited companies based in Japan as most of the used cars are imported from that country,” said Mian Shaoib Ahmed, chairman of All Pakistan Car Dealers & Importers Association. Ahmed, also a member of the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce & Industry’s (FPCCI) executive committee, stressed there was a demand for used cars in Pakistan. He contended that new Chinese entrants have yet to make their mark in Pakistani markets, while Japanese car assemblers in the country were not yet ready for the competitive environment. The FPCCI member lauded the government for recent changes in the vehicle import regime and added that used car imports under the Gift Scheme and commercial imports will continue to rise in the coming months. Ahmed referred to a notification by the Engineering Development Board (EDB), dated Sep 30, which would relax the criteria for imports of used vehicles. The changes in the recent EDB notification against the earlier notification included the removal of a clause for the minimum capital requirement of a company importing used cars, and now, any tax-registered individual or firm not even registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) can import vehicles. The pre- and post-shipment inspection will be conducted through the Pakistan Standards and Quality Control Authority (PSQCA) instead of the EDB. However, the PSQCA chief executive officer said that inspection was not done directly under or by the authority, but through its registered inspection agencies. Currently, only two local inspection agents have been registered with the PSQCA; they are the representatives of firms accredited with the Japanese Foreign Principals Inspection Agencies.
